articles.title: Cowboys complete a defensive overhaul as a stunning number of last year’s defenders are now out of the NFL
articles.standfirst: Last season, the defense gave up the most points per offensive series in franchise history
articles.summary: Last season, the defense gave up the most points per offensive series in franchise history
articles.body:
NFL teams are ready for the start of the regular season next week after their three preseason games and with the 53-man rosters announced , which as every year includes some surprises .

For the upcoming season, the youngest roster belongs to the Miami Dolphins , who are expected to be among the worst teams and to finish with a high draft pick, followed by the Cleveland Browns , where expectations are similarly low, while the Kansas City Chiefs round out the top three.

In Kansas City, however, the goal is not merely to reach the playoffs but to capture the Super Bowl after enduring their worst campaign since 2012, now with Patrick Mahomes fully healthy since Week 1.

Massive Roster Turnover Highlights Cowboys' Defensive Revolution

Like every year, one of the teams capturing the most attention when final cuts are made is the Dallas Cowboys , who are trying to end a two-year playoff drought while quarterback Dak Prescott views the upcoming campaign strictly as a Super Bowl-or-bust scenario. To achieve that ambition, the front office engineered a drastic structural overhaul on defense.

With the official 53-man roster finalized, records reveal that 17 of the 26 defenders who occupied the Cowboys' Week 1 roster last season are currently out of the NFL entirely , underscoring why the unit struggled so immensely.

Last year, Dallas allowed more than 20 points in all but one game , surrendered 30 or more points in nine separate contests , and ranked dead last in franchise history for points allowed per drive.

Ultimately, no matter how efficiently the offense performed, succeeding in the modern NFL with those types of defensive numbers proved impossible, prompting this dramatic reset.

New Faces and Rookie Talent Aim to Transform Dallas Into Contenders

To stop the bleeding, Dallas turned to new defensive coordinator Christian Parker and utilized the NFL Draft to aggressively pivot. The team spent five of their seven draft selections on defensive reinforcements, highlighted by safety Caleb Downs at 11th overall and edge rusher Malachi Lawrence at 23rd.

These roo kies step into a heavily revamped group featuring high-profile mid-season acquisition Quinnen Williams alongside veteran free-agent signings like cornerback Cobie Durant and safety Jalen Thompson .

Under head coach Brian Schottenheimer , the pressure is on to deliver immediately. Supported by an elite offensive core featuring Dak Prescott distributing the ball to CeeDee Lamb , George Pickens , and Javonte Williams , the organization finally possesses the personnel required to field an elite, balanced unit capable of conquering the brutally competitive NFC East .

articles.title: Escaping Jimmy Johnson's Shadow: An inside look at Jerry Jones' obsession with the Super Bowl
articles.standfirst: Norm Hitzges believes the Cowboys owner wants a title that cannot be credited to anyone else
articles.summary: Norm Hitzges believes the Cowboys owner wants a title that cannot be credited to anyone else
articles.body:
Jerry Jones has spent decades trying to prove the Dallas Cowboys can win on his terms, and Norm Hitzges believes that pursuit has now become deeply personal.

The longtime Dallas broadcaster says Jones ’ increasingly aggressive roster-building is about more than ending a 30-year Super Bowl drought.

In Hitzges ’ view, the Cowboys owner wants one championship that cannot be tied back to Jimmy Johnson .

“The final reason Jerry Jones might be willing to give up the future for the present: his age,” Hitzges said on Just Wondering.

“Jerry will be 84 years old in seven weeks. He, like others of us, you might call elderly, realized there’s a clock ticking.”

That clock is attached to one of the most complicated legacies in NFL history.

Jones transformed the Cowboys into a financial powerhouse, but the football side has remained frozen in one uncomfortable fact, that Dallas hasn't returned to an NFC Championship Game since its last Super Bowl-winning season.

Johnson’s fingerprints linger over Cowboys glory years

Dallas won three Super Bowls after Jones purchased the franchise, but two of those came with Johnson as head coach.

The third arrived under Barry Switzer , after Johnson had already left following a bitter power struggle with Jones . Hitzges believes that still matters.

“He won it with Barry Switzer, but it was with the remnants of the team, the Juggernaut, assembled and coached by Jimmy Johnson,” Hitzges said.

“I think that really peeves Jerry that people blame him for all the failures since then. But they think of all the successes back then as Jimmy’s and not Jerry’s.”

Johnson has long maintained that he controlled personnel decisions during the dynasty-building period, while Jones has consistently emphasized his own role in constructing the organization.

Dallas’ current approach suggests urgency

That's why the Cowboys ’ recent willingness to sacrifice future assets has caught Hitzges’ attention.

Dallas has continued to reshape its defense around established veterans while spending draft capital in an effort to maximize the current window.

Hitzges sees that strategy as evidence that Jones is no longer willing to wait.

“What’s happened since that 95 Super Bowl? They haven’t even made it to an NFC Championship game in 30 years,” he said.

“In those three decades, a total of five playoff wins. Five! The fans blame Jerry for that.

“I believe Jerry is hearing his personal clock ticking and he desperately wants to win a Super Bowl ring,” Hitzges added.

“A ring that people will think of as Jerry’s and Jerry’s alone.”

That may be the real tension surrounding Dallas in 2026. Jones has already built the richest franchise in football and secured his place among the sport’s most influential owners.

What he hasn't done is win a championship in the post-Johnson era that nobody can explain away as someone else’s team. At this stage of his career, Hitzges believes that matters more than ever.

articles.title: An insider reveals what the Dallas Cowboys' strength will be and why they could be serious contenders
articles.standfirst: Jerry Jones' team could take a major step forward with all the additions it has made.
articles.summary: Jerry Jones' team could take a major step forward with all the additions it has made.
articles.body:
D ak Prescott and CeeDee Lamb have faced their own postseason struggles, while Brian Schottenheimer , despite his extensive experience as an offensive coordinator, has yet to lead a team in a playoff game as the person in charge.

Questions remain about the Dallas Cowboys ’ ability to respond against high-level opponents in pressure-packed situations. However, before the offense or coaching staff are tested in a win-or-go-home matchup, the defense will have to prove it can help the team get there.

Cowboys believe their defense will take a leap in 2026

Dallas’ defense is coming off a difficult season. The Cowboys allowed 30.1 points per game , the worst mark in the NFL , while also giving up 251.5 passing yards per contest , the highest figure in the league. They finished 30th in total yards allowed, surrendering 377.0 yards per game .

A slight improvement could have changed the team’s outcome, but the goal for 2026 is much more ambitious: move past being one of the league’s worst defensive units and become a group capable of making a significant impact.

After adding key pieces and hiring new defensive coordinator Christian Parker, Dallas believes it can build a revamped defense. Several NFL analysts share that optimism.

“Last year, defensively, they just didn't have the horses. This year, they do,” Daniel Jeremiah of ESPN and NFL Network told The Pat McAfee Show on Monday. “{Linebacker DeMarvion Overshown} had put on some weight when I was {at training camp}. He looked great. {LB} Jaishawn Barham looked awesome… They are so much better, and then Christian Parker is outstanding as a defensive mind.

“I went and saw this with my own eyes, we're not trying to pump anything up here. This is legit a good defense to go along with what could be the best offense in football.”

Dallas began rebuilding its run defense last season with the arrival of three-time Pro Bowl selection Kenny Clark as part of the blockbuster trade involving Micah Parsons, and later strengthened the defensive line by adding former All-Pro Quinnen Williams from the New York Jets.

The Cowboys also added talent through the Draft with Caleb Downs and Jaishawn Barham, players who can contribute in multiple areas of the game. In addition, they reinforced a secondary that had shown vulnerabilities with the free-agent signings of Cobie Durant and Jalen Thompson.

Another priority was improving the pass rush, an area that struggled significantly following Parsons ’ departure.

The performance of Rashan Gary , rookie Malachi Lawrence , and future Hall of Famer Von Miller could determine this defense’s ceiling, especially if they are able to complement each other and create consistent pressure on opposing quarterbacks.

A creative defensive coordinator can maximize his players’ strengths and hide some weaknesses, and Dallas hopes Parker can be exactly that type of leader.

In his first season as defensive coordinator, Parker was part of the success of the Philadelphia Eagles , who won the Super Bowl, while leading a talented defensive backs group that included Quinyon Mitchell and Cooper DeJean . He also had the opportunity to learn under renowned defensive coordinator Vic Fangio, quickly raising his profile around the NFL.

If Parker lives up to the expectations Dallas has for him, the team’s defensive identity could change completely.

But in Dallas, there is little room for promises. Cowboys fans do not want explanations or hypothetical scenarios: they want results.

Daniel Jeremiah and other analysts believe this defense has the talent needed to deliver. Now it will have to prove it once the season begins.

articles.title: Fernando Menodza gets a boost from an insider who is rarely wrong
articles.standfirst: One of the biggest storylines in the NFL is whether the rookie quarterback will become the starter in Las Vegas.
articles.summary: One of the biggest storylines in the NFL is whether the rookie quarterback will become the starter in Las Vegas.
articles.body:
The NFL preseason has officially come to an end, and teams have now finalized their 53-man rosters ahead of Week 1 of the 2026 season, which will begin on September 9 with the defending Super Bowl champions, the Seattle Seahawks , hosting the New England Patriots .

For the Las Vegas Raiders , the new campaign will begin on September 13 at home against the Miami Dolphins , although uncertainty remains at the quarterback position. Everything points to veteran Kirk Cousins being the team’s starter to open the season, while rookie Fernando Mendoza is expected to begin his NFL career as the backup.

Adam Schefter suggests Fernando Mendoza could become the starter sooner than expected

Although Cousins appears to have the starting quarterback job secured for the beginning of the season, Adam Schefter of ESPN opened the door to the possibility that Mendoza could take over the offense earlier than expected during his appearance on The Pat McAfee Show .

“I still think it’s going to be Kirk [Cousins]. I’d be surprised if it was anybody else other than Kirk at this point in time. I think that’s the way it’s been trending all along and [Fernando] Mendoza had moments in the preseason. There’s no doubt his time is coming. He’s going to be the starter. He’s going to be the face of the franchise. The question is how soon?

“I was texting with somebody yesterday. They’re like, ‘Sooner than you think.’ I’m like, really? Now, we’ll see. … I think Cousins starts the opener against the Miami Dolphins. … I think they want to go with the veteran early in the season when there are some tough games on the schedule.”

Schefter’s comments should be taken with caution, as he did not reveal the source of that information, meaning it could simply be the opinion of someone close to the team. However, his remarks have fueled speculation that Mendoza could get his opportunity sooner than expected.

There is no question about the young quarterback’s talent, and he could potentially be ready to compete from Week 1 . However, all indications are that the Raiders prefer to take a patient approach with the player they view as the future face of the franchise rather than rushing his development.

Raiders will keep three quarterbacks on their roster

Heading into their opener against Miami, Las Vegas will carry three quarterbacks on its 53-man roster after deciding to keep Aidan O’Connell , eliminating the possibility of a trade and adding more depth at the position.

While several backup quarterbacks changed teams during the final roster adjustment period, O’Connell remained in Las Vegas — a decision that makes sense for a franchise featuring a 38-year-old veteran projected to be the starter and a rookie viewed as its long-term investment.

Now, the focus will be on determining the quarterback depth chart for Week 1: whether Mendoza will serve as Cousins’ direct backup or if new Raiders head coach Klint Kubiak will choose O’Connell as the No. 2 quarterback to begin the season.

articles.title: Jerry Jones makes controversial decision regarding Dak Prescott's Cowboys successor, surprising everyone
articles.standfirst: Dallas could lose a developing passer for nothing
articles.summary: Dallas could lose a developing passer for nothing
articles.body:
The Dallas Cowboys spent the preseason watching Joe Milton III look increasingly comfortable in their offense. Then, just as he appeared to be making his strongest case to stay, they let him go.

Dallas waived Milton on Monday to create room for running back Emari Demercado , leaving Sam Howell as the clear backup to Dak Prescott .

It was a striking decision because Milton had done almost everything the Cowboys could have asked of him during the preseason.

He completed 29 of 43 passes for 378 yards and three touchdowns without throwing an interception, showing improved accuracy and a better grasp of the offense than he had a year earlier.

Milton had also been praised internally for his development, making his release feel less like the end of a failed experiment and more like a calculated gamble.

Cowboys coach Brian Schottenheimer had suggested only recently that the competition was still unsettled.

“We're still piecing the puzzle together, and that's where this thing is very fluid,” Schottenheimer said.

Now the puzzle has been solved, at least at quarterback.

Sam Howell’s experience gave him the edge

Howell also had a productive preseason, completing 27 of 40 passes for 314 yards, three touchdowns and one interception while adding a rushing score.

What separated him most was experience. Howell has 18 career NFL starts, all with Washington, while Milton has appeared in five regular-season games and has never started.

That matters for a team with playoff expectations and an established starter in Prescott . If Dallas needs its backup for a short stretch, Howell offers a much larger sample of NFL game experience.

His contract may have also played a role. Howell signed a one-year deal worth $2.5 million guaranteed, and releasing him would still have left Dallas responsible for his $2 million base salary.

Milton , meanwhile, had no control over how the competition ultimately played out.

“That's out of my control,” Milton said during the preseason. “The only thing I'm able to do is go out there and call the play, and just make sure the offense is moving. Whatever they decide, they decide.”

Dallas risks losing developing quarterback

That's where the decision becomes more complicated. Milton wasn't simply a fringe player struggling to survive roster cuts. He had shown real progress and looked increasingly capable of becoming a dependable NFL backup.

The Cowboys reportedly explored trade possibilities involving him before finalizing the roster but didn't find a deal. Now he must pass through waivers.

If another team claims him, Dallas loses a developmental quarterback who appeared to be trending upward. If he clears, the Cowboys could potentially bring him back on the practice squad.

Milton himself believed the offense was beginning to come naturally.

“You get to do a lot more,” he said. “Just being able to go through that process of a whole year being in this offense to now, it's great.”

Howell may be the safer choice today. The unanswered question is whether Dallas just gave away the quarterback with more room to grow tomorrow.

articles.title: The shattered dream of Shiyazh Pete, the first Navajo player in the NFL: the Cowboys, merciless after his locker room video
articles.standfirst: The Dallas Cowboys have terminated the contract of offensive lineman Shiyazh Pete, the first Navajo to sign with an NFL team.
articles.summary: The Dallas Cowboys have terminated the contract of offensive lineman Shiyazh Pete, the first Navajo to sign with an NFL team.
articles.body:
Shiyazh Pete seemed to be living the beginning of a perfect story. The young offensive lineman had made history by becoming the first member of the Navajo Nation to sign with an NFL team.

However, the Dallas Cowboys had to reduce their roster to the 53-player limit, and Pete was one of the names left out. The player who had thrilled an entire locker room and won over thousands of fans now once again faces uncertainty.

The video that turned Shiyazh Pete into a sensation

The moment that put Pete at the center of everyone's attention came during the preseason game against the Arizona Cardinals .

Pooh Bear thrilled his teammates, won over social media, and starred in one of the most special moments in the NFL . A large number of Navajo fans came to the stadium to support him, and the player received a standing ovation that even surprised the coach.

The athlete starred in a scene that quickly went viral when, after head coach Brian Schottenheimer, asked him to deliver a speech in the Cowboys locker room, he gave a rallying talk that won over social media and the hearts of those who were able to hear it.

The message spoke about the path they had traveled together and the brotherhood that football can create. The speech sparked an enormous reaction within the team, and the video ended up becoming a sensation on social media.

From a locker room hero to being left off the roster

In contrast to what happened, the story took a much harsher turn for the NFL star. The Cowboys made their final moves to reach the definitive 53-man roster, Pete was cut by Dallas and became a free agent.

The contrast could not have been greater: just a few days earlier, his teammates were celebrating his words in the locker room and thousands of people were sharing his story. Now, the player who became a symbol for the Navajo community will have to wait for a new opportunity.

His departure from the Cowboys does not necessarily mean the end of his journey. As a free agent, Pete can sign with another NFL team and could also find an opportunity on a practice squad.

Pete was born on the Flathead Indian Reservation in Roanan, Montana . According to the El Paso Times, he began playing football in seventh grade before transferring to Shiprock High School in New Mexico during his sophomore year.

This story once again showed that even if you build the most powerful story, even if everything seems like a perfect tale, nothing guarantees you a place on the team the next day.

Pete could still join the Dallas practice squad if he is not claimed by another team.

articles.title: Who is Savanna Dastrup? The new Dallas Cowboys cheerleader that was rejected last year
articles.standfirst: The 23-year-old refused to quit after 2025 and turned one of her toughest moments into a career breakthrough
articles.summary: The 23-year-old refused to quit after 2025 and turned one of her toughest moments into a career breakthrough
articles.body:
S avanna Dastrup knows exactly how close a dream can feel before it disappears.

Last year, the Utah native reached Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders training camp and came within days of earning a roster spot, only to be cut before the final team was announced. Instead of walking away, she treated the rejection as proof that she was close enough to come back and finish the job.

“I actually auditioned last year, made it through training camp and got cut, like, the week before the team was made,” Dastrup said. “It was super hard, super devastating. But it really motivated me to come back and work harder. And it meant that much more.”

That decision paid off in 2026.

Dastrup returned for another audition, survived training camp and finally earned the place she had been chasing since she was a teenager.

“I wasn’t going to stop either,” she said. “If it wasn’t this year, I was going to audition again.”

Her Dallas Cowboys dream started at 14

Dastrup grew up in Orem, Utah, and first became obsessed with the Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders after watching “Making the Team” with her mother.

“My mom was like, ‘You should watch Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders: Making the Team with me,’” she said. “So I watched it and I was like, ‘That’s what I want to do.’”

She began taking DCC prep classes at 15 and later chose Texas Christian University in part because Dallas was close enough to keep pursuing the goal.

Dastrup danced with the TCU Showgirls throughout college while regularly making the trip to Dallas for additional prep classes.

Her first full attempt in 2025 was documented during “America’s Sweethearts: Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders.” She reached training camp in an unusually competitive year but eventually became one of the cuts.

DCC director Kelli Finglass encouraged her not to give up.

“You might just chalk this up to timing and experience and the pressure,” Finglass told her. “But I think you've got the skills to make this team or another team.”

Dastrup turned rejection into a second chance

After the setback, Dastrup spent time studying fashion in Paris and continued teaching dance before returning for the 2026 auditions.

This time, the outcome changed.

“I can’t even believe it still,” Dastrup said. “I’m so used to coming and being like, ‘Am I going to get cut tonight?’ I think I still am trying to get out of that mindset. Like, Savanna, you made it.”

She credits her family with helping her stay committed throughout the process.

“My dad always told me to be the first at the studio, the last to leave - put in the extra work - and what’s meant to be will be,” she said.

Now, Dastrup is preparing for the moment she once thought might never arrive.

Her message to anyone dealing with the same kind of rejection is simple.

“I hope that girls that get rejected or don’t make the team they want realize there is a bigger picture,” she said. “And just, yeah, don’t give up.”

One year ago, Dastrup left training camp without a roster spot.

Now she is proof that getting cut does not always mean the dream is over.

“I wasn’t going to stop either,” she said. “If it wasn’t this year, I was going to audition again.”
Her Dallas Cowboys dream started at 14
Dastrup grew up in Orem, Utah, and first became obsessed with the Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders after watching “Making the Team” with her mother.
“My mom was like, ‘You should watch Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders: Making the Team with me,’” she said. “So I watched it and I was like, ‘That’s what I want to do.’”
She began taking DCC prep classes at 15 and later chose Texas Christian University in part because Dallas was close enough to keep pursuing the goal.
Dastrup danced with the TCU Showgirls throughout college while regularly making the trip to Dallas for additional prep classes.

Her first full attempt in 2025 was documented during “America’s Sweethearts: Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders.” She reached training camp in an unusually competitive year but eventually became one of the cuts.
DCC director Kelli Finglass encouraged her not to give up.
“You might just chalk this up to timing and experience and the pressure,” Finglass told her. “But I think you've got the skills to make this team or another team.”
Dastrup turned rejection into a second chance
After the setback, Dastrup spent time studying fashion in Paris and continued teaching dance before returning for the 2026 auditions.
This time, the outcome changed.

“I can’t even believe it still,” Dastrup said. “I’m so used to coming and being like, ‘Am I going to get cut tonight?’ I think I still am trying to get out of that mindset. Like, Savanna, you made it.”
She credits her family with helping her stay committed throughout the process.
“My dad always told me to be the first at the studio, the last to leave - put in the extra work - and what’s meant to be will be,” she said.
Now, Dastrup is preparing for the moment she once thought might never arrive.
Her message to anyone dealing with the same kind of rejection is simple.
“I hope that girls that get rejected or don’t make the team they want realize there is a bigger picture,” she said. “And just, yeah, don’t give up.”
One year ago, Dastrup left training camp without a roster spot.
Now she is proof that getting cut does not always mean the dream is over.

articles.title: Former NFL player lashes out at Jerry Jones' latest decision: “Sam Howell is trash, like dumpster trash”
articles.standfirst: Roddy White questions Dallas' choice to keep Howell over Joe Milton after the young quarterback impressed throughout the preseason
articles.summary: Roddy White questions Dallas' choice to keep Howell over Joe Milton after the young quarterback impressed throughout the preseason
articles.body:
The Dallas Cowboys ' decision to part ways with Joe Milton after initially including him on their 53-man roster has sparked a strong reaction from former NFL wide receiver Roddy White .

Milton's departure came as something of a surprise after the quarterback produced an impressive preseason campaign and appeared to have made a strong case to serve as Dak Prescott 's backup.

Instead, Dallas retained Sam Howell and subsequently waived Milton to create room for running back Emari Demercado .

White , who spent the majority of his NFL career with the Atlanta Falcons , made his frustration clear on social media. He argued that Milton's performances should have been enough to earn him a place on the roster.

“How the hell Joe Milton get cut. He literally dominated the whole preseason,” White wrote on X. “ Sam Howell is trash like dumpster trash.”

The blunt assessment immediately put the Cowboys ' quarterback decision under additional scrutiny.

While White's comments were particularly forceful, Milton's preseason numbers provide some explanation for why the move caught attention.

The 26-year-old completed 29 of his 43 attempts for 378 yards, three touchdowns and zero interceptions during the preseason. Those figures made him one of the more efficient quarterbacks competing for the backup role.

Milton joined Dallas last season after arriving in a trade with the New England Patriots . His opportunities were limited in his first season with the Cowboys, as he appeared in only four games and finished with 183 passing yards, one touchdown and two interceptions.

His development this summer, however, appeared to change the conversation around his future.

Why the Cowboys ultimately chose Howell

Howell's situation was complicated by both his preseason performances and his contract. The quarterback had $2.5 million guaranteed, including a $2 million base salary, meaning Dallas would have remained responsible for the guaranteed money even if it had decided to move on from him.

That financial reality likely played a role in the final decision.

Howell also produced his best stretch of preseason football in the finale against the New Orleans Saints . After opening the second half with a three-and-out that ended with a sack, he responded with a 52-yard completion to Jordan Hudson .

He then found Hudson for a 26-yard touchdown on the opening play of the fourth quarter. Howell subsequently engineered a 12-play, 67-yard scoring drive, which ended with Mitch Van Voren finding the end zone from 21 yards out. Howell added the two-point conversion himself, helping Dallas pull level.

That late performance may have strengthened Howell's position, even as Milton's overall preseason body of work appeared stronger.

Milton had also received praise from other former NFL players. Asante Samuel previously suggested that the quarterback could give Dallas another dimension if Prescott were forced to miss time.

“The Dallas Cowboys are gonna end up winning the NFC East. It’s just my prediction. I still expect them to be that good if Joe Milton does end up having to take over for some unfortunate reason, some unfortunate circumstances,” Samuel said on his podcast, Say What Needs to be Said.

“That probably will increase the Cowboys ’ chances of getting further in the playoffs. It’s just another way of saying Joe Milton III brings more to the table than Dak Prescott .”

Milton's physical tools also drew a comparison to former NFL MVP Cam Newton during Dallas' joint practice with New Orleans, adding to the sense that the quarterback had generated considerable momentum.

Still, the Cowboys ' decision may not necessarily represent the end of Milton's time in Dallas.

Because Milton has not yet accumulated enough service time to become a vested veteran, he must pass through waivers before he can become a free agent. If no team claims him, Dallas could bring him back on its practice squad.

That possibility makes the timing of the move particularly intriguing. Star-Telegram reporter Nick Harris suggested the Cowboys may have deliberately waited until after the initial roster deadline so fewer teams would have an immediate need at quarterback.

“I’m chalking up the timing of the Joe Milton III release to roster/waiver strategy,” Harris wrote on X. “Release him on Sunday, much higher chance he gets claimed. Release him today, a lot of teams have their QB situations figured out, making it more likely he clears waivers. Just my take.”

ESPN also reported that Dallas explored trade possibilities involving Milton before the 53-man deadline.

For now, Howell remains the Cowboys ' No. 2 quarterback, while Milton's next destination remains uncertain.

White's criticism may have been unusually harsh, but it reflects a wider debate surrounding a decision that came after Milton seemingly did everything possible to strengthen his case.

If Milton clears waivers and returns to Dallas' practice squad, the Cowboys could still have an opportunity to continue developing the talented young quarterback. If another team claims him, however, Dallas may quickly discover whether moving on from him was the right call.

articles.title: Tony Romo makes first claim on alcohol dependence in statement after DUI arrest
articles.standfirst: The former Cowboys QB is taking responsibility while focusing on his health and family
articles.summary: The former Cowboys QB is taking responsibility while focusing on his health and family
articles.body:
Tony Romo has opened up after being arrested for driving under the influence of alcohol in July, taking responsibility for what happened months ago and addressing the personal struggles behind the incident.

Romo used football as a way to speak openly about his situation and acknowledge the mistake he made . He explained that difficult moments in his life led him to become dependent on medication, and that after trying to stop taking it, he developed a dependence on alcohol.

His struggles began after NFL career ended earlier than he wanted

According to Romo, multiple surgeries forced his career to end sooner than he would have liked , leaving him with debilitating pain. He stressed that none of this excuses his actions, but decided it was time to address the circumstances that contributed to the behavior shown during his arrest.

Although the situation could be embarrassing, Romo chose to take responsibility and speak honestly as he works to continue being a good example for his three children . He also wants to use the experience to teach them a lesson that came from a difficult period in his life.

Romo is working with doctors as he looks to make a healthier change

Romo also revealed that he is working with a team of doctors to make the necessary changes to maintain a much healthier life . He said his family, friends and the NFL community have motivated him throughout the process , while also asking for privacy after his situation suddenly became public.

CBS Sports placed its lead NFL analyst on leave until further notice on July 31. The network later said there was no timetable for a decision regarding Romo’s future, with J.J. Watt taking his place alongside Jim Nantz and Tracy Wolfson on CBS’ lead NFL broadcast team.

Romo did not provide a timetable for his return to CBS, but made clear that he hopes to return to broadcasting after taking time to focus on his health and family.

The statement marks the first time Romo has publicly detailed the personal struggles he says led to the Wisconsin incident. After more than two decades in football, including 14 seasons with the Cowboys before beginning his broadcasting career at CBS, Romo said he is approaching this latest chapter by applying the lessons he learned from the game.

articles.title: Jerry Jones' relationship with Dak Prescott seems to be a lifelong one: he'll be a Cowboy for life
articles.standfirst: Dallas appears to have no immediate succession plan at quarterback as Prescott enters another season as the unquestioned face of the franchise
articles.summary: Dallas appears to have no immediate succession plan at quarterback as Prescott enters another season as the unquestioned face of the franchise
articles.body:
D ak Prescott 's future with the Dallas Cowboys appears to be about as secure as it gets in the NFL .

While quarterback situations can change quickly across the league, there is little indication that Dallas is preparing for life after Prescott anytime soon.

In fact, Cowboys insider Clarence Hill Jr. believes the organization has effectively made its intentions clear by failing to establish a developmental quarterback capable of eventually taking over.

Hill offered a blunt assessment of the situation as Dallas prepared for the 2026 season.

" Dak Prescott will be the Cowboys quarterback for years to come," Hill tweeted. "There is no succession plan, no developmental option in place."

That statement is particularly notable following Dallas' latest quarterback decision. The Cowboys initially carried both Sam Howell and Joe Milton alongside Prescott on their 53-man roster, but Milton was subsequently waived after the team added running back Emari Demercado . Howell ultimately remained Prescott's backup.

The move raised eyebrows because Milton had enjoyed an encouraging preseason. He completed 29 of 43 passes for 378 yards and three touchdowns without throwing an interception, prompting some observers to believe he could eventually develop into a legitimate option behind Prescott .

Instead, Dallas chose Howell , whose previous NFL experience and guaranteed contract strengthened his position.

The decision reinforced the idea that the Cowboys are focused on Prescott as their immediate and longer-term answer rather than actively grooming a successor.

Jerry Jones has repeatedly backed Prescott

The relationship between Prescott and Cowboys owner Jerry Jones has been built over a decade.

Prescott arrived in Dallas as a fourth-round pick in 2016 and unexpectedly became the starter after Tony Romo suffered a preseason injury. Rather than simply filling in temporarily, Prescott took control of the position and established himself as the franchise quarterback.

His career has since included multiple Pro Bowl selections, a second-team All-Pro honor and the 2022 Walter Payton NFL Man of the Year award. He also became the Cowboys' all-time leading passer, further cementing his place in franchise history.

Jones ' commitment became particularly clear when Dallas handed Prescott a four-year, $240 million contract extension in 2025, with $231 million guaranteed.

That financial commitment makes it difficult to imagine the Cowboys abruptly moving away from Prescott unless circumstances change dramatically.

The current quarterback depth chart only strengthens that conclusion. Rather than selecting a young quarterback specifically designed to learn behind Prescott , Dallas has opted for experienced depth in Howell.

Milton's release also means there is no obvious young successor sitting directly behind the veteran starter.

That does not necessarily mean Dallas will never draft Prescott's replacement. NFL teams can change direction quickly, and the quarterback position is particularly vulnerable to injuries and performance fluctuations.

But Hill's assessment reflects what the Cowboys ' current construction suggests: there is no urgency to identify the next face of the offense. For Prescott, that represents another significant vote of confidence.

At 33 years old, he remains the centerpiece of Dallas' plans heading into the 2026 campaign. The Cowboys ' decision-making around the quarterback room suggests that, for now, the organization would rather maximize the remainder of Prescott's career than spend resources preparing for the era that follows him.

And with Jones still firmly attached to the franchise and Prescott tied to Dallas financially and structurally, the relationship between quarterback and owner looks set to continue for years.

Whether that eventually translates into the postseason success the Cowboys expect is another question. But as far as Prescott's place in Dallas is concerned, the message appears unmistakable: the Cowboys are still building around Dak.

articles.title: Cowboys legend Emmitt Smith faces legal trouble over alleged $2.5M fraud case
articles.standfirst: A shocking legal controversy is surrounding one of the greatest players in Cowboys history.
articles.summary: A shocking legal controversy is surrounding one of the greatest players in Cowboys history.
articles.body:
The Dallas Cowboys built an NFL dynasty with Emmitt Smith as one of their greatest stars. However, the legendary running back and Pro Football Hall of Fame member is now facing a serious legal issue after being accused of allegedly participating in a fraud scheme tied to a $2.5 million investment .

According to Front Office Sports , Smith has been accused of defrauding an investor from a Native American community .

"Ex-NFL star Emmitt Smith is accused of cheating a Native American investor out of $2.5M. He (and) the other defendants allegedly used money meant to fund a Texas solar project to instead pay back a company that had previously invested in his ventures," Front Office Sports reported on X , formerly Twitter .

Emmitt Smith faces lawsuit over alleged fraud

The lawsuit centers on 4 13 Solutions , a real estate and energy company co-founded by Smith and businessman David Mosley .

According to Courthouse News Service , the company pitched Kituwah LLC , the business arm of the Eastern Band of Cherokee Indians , on an investment opportunity in early 2023 .

The lawsuit alleges that Kituwah invested $2.5 million to finance a solar energy project in Texas . However, it claims those funds were instead used to pay off the company's prior financial obligations and that the investor never received the promised returns. As a result, the group is seeking compensation for the damages.

The legal proceedings are still in their early stages, and the direction of the case is expected to become clearer in the coming months.

Emmitt Smith won three Super Bowl championships with the Dallas Cowboys and became the NFL's all-time leading rusher . After his highly successful tenure in Dallas, he spent the final seasons of his career with the Arizona Cardinals before retiring in 2004.

Since then, the former running back has remained a prominent figure around the NFL and the Cowboys, working as an analyst and appearing as a guest on various nationally televised sports programs.

articles.title: George Pickens can dominate NFL defenses, but his Cowboys teammates exposed his golf struggles
articles.standfirst: It appears that golf is not exactly his strong suit for the star wide receiver.
articles.summary: It appears that golf is not exactly his strong suit for the star wide receiver.
articles.body:
The Dallas Cowboys wide receiver went viral after a funny moment during a trip to Utah with several of his teammates, including Dak Prescott , one of the biggest golf enthusiasts on the team.

In the video, Pickens grabs the club and prepares for his tee shot… but completely misses the ball. His unusual swing had his teammates bursting into laughter, while Prescott took the opportunity to joke with him and even offer some advice to improve his technique.

The good news for Pickens is that Dak’s tips worked. On his next attempt, the receiver made solid contact and sent the ball a good distance, avoiding an even more embarrassing moment.

Fans did not hold back on Pickens

The video quickly sparked a wave of comments and jokes from fans:

“Golf doesn’t care even a little bit how athletic you are, and George Pickens just found that out on camera,” one user wrote on X.

Others compared his swing to a video game character or to the moves of amateur golfers who play at local courses.

But away from the golf course, Pickens remains one of the most important pieces of Dallas’ offense. In his first season with the Cowboys, he led the team in receptions with 93 catches, 1,429 receiving yards and nine touchdowns.

Despite his impressive production, the wide receiver was unable to reach a contract extension with Dallas during the offseason and will play the season under the franchise tag. If the Cowboys do not reach a new deal or decide to trade him, Pickens could become a free agent in March.

For now, the Cowboys can breathe easy: their star appears to be much more focused on catching passes from Dak Prescott than trying to become the next big name in golf.

articles.title: It's crazy what the Cowboys are doing with Joe Milton: Now no one can sign him
articles.standfirst: The young quarterback drew interest from around the NFL, but his future took an unexpected turn after hitting waivers.
articles.summary: The young quarterback drew interest from around the NFL, but his future took an unexpected turn after hitting waivers.
articles.body:
The Dallas Cowboys decided to give the rest of the NFL a chance to claim quarterback Joe Milton by placing him on the waiver wire during the team’s final roster cuts. However, just a few days later, the young quarterback returned to Dallas, leaving other teams without the opportunity to sign him.

The Cowboys announced Milton’s addition to the practice squad after no team in the league claimed him.

“The Cowboys have signed QB Joe Milton to the practice squad,” Tommy Yarish of Cowboys.com reported through his official X account.

Meanwhile, Jon Machota of The Athletic confirmed the move: “Joe Milton has been signed to the Cowboys’ practice squad.”

NFL insider Jordan Schultz added that the 26-year-old quarterback drew interest from several teams, but his priority was remaining in Dallas.

“Sources: The Cowboys are signing QB Joe Milton to their PS. The talented 26-year-old drew interest from most NFL teams but wanted to stay in Dallas.”

Cowboys cut Joe Milton to finalize their 53-man roster

Dallas released Milton as part of its final roster moves to trim the team down to 53 players ahead of the regular-season opener against the New York Giants on September 13.

“Source: Cowboys are releasing QB Joe Milton,” reported Adam Schefter of ESPN.

Milton’s temporary departure left Sam Howell , the former starting quarterback for the Washington Commanders, as Dak Prescott’s primary backup heading into the start of the season.

“Milton would be eligible for the practice squad if he clears waivers. Sam Howell is the No. 2 QB behind Dak Prescott,” Todd Archer of ESPN explained.

NFL reporter Aaron Wilson also confirmed that the Cowboys officially placed Milton on waivers.

A fierce battle to become Dak Prescott’s backup

Milton and Howell engaged in a competitive battle throughout organized team activities (OTAs) and training camp for the role of Prescott’s backup.

Howell enters the season with starting experience after opening 17 games for the Commanders in 2024, while Milton was trying to earn an opportunity thanks to his physical tools and elite arm strength.

In May, Todd Archer of ESPN identified Milton as one of Dallas’ players with the most to prove heading into minicamp.

“Acquired last year in a trade with the New England Patriots , Milton impressed with his arm strength during the spring and the early stages of training camp,” Archer wrote.

During the 2025 season, Milton appeared in four games, completing 15 of 24 passes for 183 yards , with one touchdown and two interceptions. The Cowboys also strengthened the quarterback competition by signing Howell in free agency with a $2 million guarantee .

Now, Milton will have another opportunity on the practice squad, where he will continue developing and look to prove he can be a reliable option behind Dak Prescott.

Dallas released Milton as part of its final roster moves to trim the team down to 53 players ahead of the regular-season opener against the New York Giants on September 13.
“Source: Cowboys are releasing QB Joe Milton,” reported Adam Schefter of ESPN.
Milton’s temporary departure left Sam Howell , the former starting quarterback for the Washington Commanders, as Dak Prescott’s primary backup heading into the start of the season.
“Milton would be eligible for the practice squad if he clears waivers. Sam Howell is the No. 2 QB behind Dak Prescott,” Todd Archer of ESPN explained.
NFL reporter Aaron Wilson also confirmed that the Cowboys officially placed Milton on waivers.
A fierce battle to become Dak Prescott’s backup
Milton and Howell engaged in a competitive battle throughout organized team activities (OTAs) and training camp for the role of Prescott’s backup.

Howell enters the season with starting experience after opening 17 games for the Commanders in 2024, while Milton was trying to earn an opportunity thanks to his physical tools and elite arm strength.
In May, Todd Archer of ESPN identified Milton as one of Dallas’ players with the most to prove heading into minicamp.
“Acquired last year in a trade with the New England Patriots , Milton impressed with his arm strength during the spring and the early stages of training camp,” Archer wrote.

During the 2025 season, Milton appeared in four games, completing 15 of 24 passes for 183 yards , with one touchdown and two interceptions. The Cowboys also strengthened the quarterback competition by signing Howell in free agency with a $2 million guarantee .
Now, Milton will have another opportunity on the practice squad, where he will continue developing and look to prove he can be a reliable option behind Dak Prescott.

articles.title: A Cowboys legend believes Brian Schottenheimer has changed the team’s culture
articles.standfirst: The Cowboys made a decision that shocked the NFL. Now, a franchise legend believes Brian Schottenheimer has changed the team’s culture in a way few expected.
articles.summary: The Cowboys made a decision that shocked the NFL. Now, a franchise legend believes Brian Schottenheimer has changed the team’s culture in a way few expected.
articles.body:
When the Dallas Cowboys surprised the NFL by promoting Brian Schottenheimer as their head coach in 2025 instead of pursuing a more established name from outside the organization, the decision raised questions among fans and analysts.

The Cowboys have full confidence in the evolution of their offense

While some believed the franchise avoided paying a high price for a marquee coach, others argued that continuity with Schottenheimer could be the key, especially after Dallas’ offense showed promising signs under his leadership.

Now, with Schottenheimer entering his second year in charge, the perception inside the organization appears to have changed. During an appearance on The Rich Eisen Show , Cowboys legend Michael Irvin praised the coach’s work and said the team’s culture has taken a positive turn in 2026.

“I’m so happy with the decision that they made… to hire him. Because I was like, man, we need somebody from outside coming in to change the whole culture, but he has changed the culture there. And people, you know, he’s changed the culture in such a way that I think now, here from here on, it goes different,” Irvin said.

The former wide receiver also highlighted how the arrival of players with experience elsewhere has helped change the mindset inside the locker room, using George Pickens as an example.

“And I believe, Rich, what has happened is an outsider came in to show everybody how blessed you are to be with the Cowboys. George Pickens making the decision that you just talked about to say, ‘Hey, wait a minute, I’ve been other places. I know how great this is. See, all the other people, you guys have never been other places.’ So you just, you’re spoiled with this. But the decision George Pickens made, I think it’s a galvanizing decision. A decision that says, ‘Oh, we must really have something great.’ If he didn’t go through that.”

Although Dallas did not win more games in Schottenheimer’s first season than they did in Mike McCarthy ’s final year, the team’s offensive performance showed significant improvement. The Cowboys went from finishing 2024 ranked 11th in passing offense and 27th in rushing offense to becoming the second-best passing offense and ninth-best rushing offense in 2025.

Additionally, the arrival of Christian Parker as the new defensive coordinator and the implementation of a system influenced by Vic Fangio ’s defensive scheme have raised expectations surrounding the team.

After years of falling short in their pursuit of a championship, the Cowboys are generating optimism once again. If the offensive growth continues and the revamped defense takes another step forward, 2026 could finally be the year Dallas returns to the NFL’s elite contenders.

articles.title: Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders make fans furious and demand an immediate response from Jerry Jones
articles.standfirst: Billions for the franchise. Millions for the stars. But what about the Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders?
articles.summary: Billions for the franchise. Millions for the stars. But what about the Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders?
articles.body:
The Dallas Cowboys are the most valuable sports franchise in the world. If Jerry Jones decided to sell “America’s Team,” he could potentially receive more than $20 billion . As a reference point, if the Los Angeles Lakers reached a valuation of nearly $12 billion , the NFL’s most iconic franchise could approach twice that amount thanks to its immense popularity and brand power.

However, while the Cowboys’ value is measured in billions of dollars, there is a significant gap when it comes to the earnings of their cheerleaders, who continue to make far less compared to the team’s players.

While Dallas’ top stars receive contracts worth tens of millions of dollars per season, members of the Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders earn, at best, tens of thousands of dollars per year.

How much do Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders make?

According to multiple reports, the Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders can earn up to $2,500 per game and make between $50,000 and $75,000 per season.

Although that figure may seem substantial for a part-time job, the reality is that for many members of the squad, the role requires a much greater commitment, including practices, promotional events, public appearances, and brand-related obligations.

“This will be year two of the ‘Boys cheerleaders making a reported 400% increase in salary compared to a previous salary scale. The new scale is said to pay $75/hr compared to $15/hour in previous years. While exact numbers aren’t public record, based on what cheerleaders have revealed via Netflix’s America’s Sweethearts series, experts believe the veteran cheerleaders can make $50k to $75k per season, including a rate of $2,500 per game based on the $75/hr. figure,” Fox News reported.

NFL fans call for better pay for Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders

The difference between the franchise’s value and the cheerleaders’ earnings has sparked debate among NFL fans , who believe they should receive compensation that better reflects the importance of the brand they represent.

Many fans took to social media to make their voices heard, including messages directed at Jerry Jones, asking him to increase their pay.

Jerry Jones has never hesitated to invest heavily in his biggest stars. Players such as Dak Prescott, Ezekiel Elliott, CeeDee Lamb, and Tony Romo have all received lucrative contracts during their time with the Cowboys.

Now, some fans believe the Dallas owner should apply that same philosophy to the Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders, one of the most recognizable and popular brands within the organization.

articles.title: Dak Prescott’s unfiltered mentality sets high-stakes ultimatum for 2026
articles.standfirst: The Cowboys QB isn’t looking for a reset. He’s focused on becoming a smarter, better leader.
articles.summary: The Cowboys QB isn’t looking for a reset. He’s focused on becoming a smarter, better leader.
articles.body:
D ak Prescott is not looking to reinvent himself heading into the 2026 NFL season . The Dallas Cowboys quarterback understands that his next step is about improving his mental approach to the game and making better decisions on the field.

According to Jon Machota of The Athletic , Prescott explained that his main area of improvement is related to reading the game and understanding how every play impacts the rest of the team.

“Every part of the game. I just think the more that you play, sometimes it gets easier to see things coming. But that doesn’t allow me to know exactly what’s about to happen. So really just staying in the moment, staying where my feet are, not trying to hit a home run each and every play. But just playing the play individually, understanding that every decision I make has an effect on the whole team. So it’s not just one area.”

That mindset is exactly what the Cowboys expect from their offensive leader. Although Prescott had an impressive individual season in 2025, throwing for 4,552 passing yards and 30 touchdowns while starting all 17 regular-season games , his production was not enough to lead Dallas to the playoffs.

The Cowboys finished with a 7-9-1 record and once again missed the postseason despite having one of the league’s most talented offenses.

With CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens forming one of the NFL’s most explosive receiving duos, along with the return of running back Javonte Williams , who rushed for more than 1,200 yards last season , Prescott knows Dallas has the weapons needed to compete.

However, the quarterback understands that statistics are no longer enough.

“Last year was a good year, but I want to be better than that,” Prescott said.

For Dallas to return to playoff contention, Prescott will need to turn his impressive individual numbers into team success. The veteran quarterback’s evolution will depend on his ability to control the game and make the right decisions in critical moments.

articles.title: Brian Schottenheimer spills the truth on Joe Milton’s shocking roster reversal
articles.standfirst: Joe Milton survived the Cowboys’ roster cuts, and Brian Schottenheimer revealed why Dallas wasn’t ready to let him go.
articles.summary: Joe Milton survived the Cowboys’ roster cuts, and Brian Schottenheimer revealed why Dallas wasn’t ready to let him go.
articles.body:
The Dallas Cowboys are already focused on the start of the 2026 NFL season . After finalizing their roster, head coach Brian Schottenheimer is turning his attention to the final details of the game plan ahead of Week 1 . Among the players who survived the final roster cuts is quarterback Joe Milton , who will continue developing within the Dallas organization.

Brian Schottenheimer excited to have Joe Milton back

Milton’s powerful arm remains one of the most intriguing aspects of his game. Although he has yet to earn the opportunity to become a full-time starting quarterback in the NFL, his physical tools have impressed both coaches and fans, and Schottenheimer believes having a player with his skill set is valuable for the Cowboys’ future.

“Cowboys coach Brian Schottenheimer is ‘elated’ to have QB Joe Milton on the practice squad. ‘We’re thrilled to get him back. He’s gonna continue to get better,’” The Athletic’s Jon Machota reported on Thursday .

Milton was selected by the New England Patriots in the sixth round of the 2024 NFL Draft and quickly generated excitement after a strong preseason performance, where he showcased his ability to make deep throws and utilize his elite arm strength. However, he appeared in only one regular-season game during his time in New England.

In April 2025, the Patriots traded Milton to the Dallas Cowboys , where he received more opportunities to gain NFL experience. The quarterback appeared in four games with Dallas, although he never earned a starting role. Still, those reps represented valuable experience as he continued adjusting to the speed and demands of professional football.

Joe Milton chooses to continue his development in Dallas

After being waived during the final roster moves in August, Milton had the opportunity to explore options with another franchise. Instead, the quarterback chose to remain with the Cowboys by re-signing with the practice squad, a move that was welcomed by Schottenheimer and the coaching staff.

Milton’s development will be one of the storylines to monitor throughout the season. His physical abilities, especially his rare arm strength, give him intriguing potential as Dallas continues to invest in his growth as a quarterback.

The Cowboys will open the 2026 NFL season on September 13 , when they face Jaxson Dart and the New York Giants in the first game of a new campaign.

articles.title: Cowboys reunion: Dak Prescott details why Joe Milton’s return boosts Dallas quarterback room
articles.standfirst: Cowboys keep Joe Milton after waiver scare as Dak Prescott praises his potential
articles.summary: Cowboys keep Joe Milton after waiver scare as Dak Prescott praises his potential
articles.body:
Dak Prescott couldn’t hide his excitement after the Dallas Cowboys brought Joe Milton back, giving the quarterback room another talented arm heading into the 2026 season.

Milton was waived after losing the battle with Sam Howell for the backup quarterback job. Dallas ultimately chose Howell, whose experience and consistency gave him the edge, but the Cowboys weren’t prepared to completely move on from Milton .

After clearing waivers, Milton returned to Dallas on the practice squad, restoring the team’s three-quarterback setup. That was welcome news for Prescott .

The Cowboys quarterback admitted he expected another team to claim Milton , making his return something of a bonus for Dallas. Prescott believes Milton can make the quarterback room stronger while continuing to develop into a player with considerable potential.

"It means a lot," Prescott said. "Obviously, me just personally, I thought he would've gotten picked up in the waivers. Fortunate for us, we got a hell of a player back and a guy that makes our room better, a guy that makes our team better.

“His spirit, just the way that he approaches the day… he's a hell of a dude, a hell of a competitor."

Prescott wants to help Milton keep developing

As Dallas’ leader and starting quarterback, Prescott understands that the young signal-caller could benefit from guidance, especially after missing out on the backup position.

Losing a competition can be frustrating, but Prescott wants Milton to avoid allowing that disappointment to derail his progress. Instead, he wants the quarterback to use the experience as motivation and continue working toward his long-term goals.

That support could be particularly important given Milton’s limited NFL experience. The former sixth-round pick has appeared in only five regular-season games during his first two professional seasons, so every opportunity to learn within an NFL environment matters.

Head coach Brian Schottenheimer was also delighted that Milton stayed with the organization. The coach has praised the quarterback’s work ethic and development, while highlighting the rare physical talent that made Dallas interested in him in the first place.

“When he informed me he’s coming back, I was elated,” Schottenheimer said. “This is a guy that’s worked his butt off to get where he is, developed the way he’s developed. The talent is so rare.”

Milton’s preseason performance also gave the Cowboys plenty to like. He completed 29 of 43 passes for 378 yards and three touchdowns without throwing an interception, while also contributing a rushing touchdown. Those numbers helped demonstrate why Dallas didn’t want to risk losing him permanently.

Howell , meanwhile, earned the official QB2 role after a competitive battle. His previous starting experience gives Dallas a more proven option behind Prescott , and he’s expected to contribute throughout the week by helping prepare for opposing defenses and providing another perspective in meetings.

Keeping all three quarterbacks could prove useful for Dallas as the season progresses. Injuries can quickly change a team's plans at the position, and having Milton already familiar with the offense gives the Cowboys an additional option without starting his development from scratch.

articles.title: Dak Prescott reacts to Jerry Jones' sudden roster move following Brian Schottenheimer's call
articles.standfirst: The Cowboys brought Joe Milton back after waivers, and Prescott believes Dallas retained a player with significant upside
articles.summary: The Cowboys brought Joe Milton back after waivers, and Prescott believes Dallas retained a player with significant upside
articles.body:
Dallas kept another developmental quarterback in the building after Brian Schottenheimer made his preference clear, and Dak Prescott believes the decision could pay off.

The Cowboys waived Joe Milton while setting their initial 53-man roster, choosing Sam Howell as Prescott ’s primary backup.

But Schottenheimer wanted Milton back if the 26-year-old cleared waivers, and owner Jerry Jones followed through by re-signing him to the practice squad. Prescott didn't hide his approval.

“It means a lot,” Prescott said. “Just me, personally, I thought he would’ve been picked up in the waivers or whatever it is. Fortunate for us, we got a hell of a player back and a guy that makes our room better, a guy that makes our team better.”

Milton ’s arm talent has long been the most obvious part of his game, but Prescott pointed to more than that when explaining why Dallas was fortunate to retain him.

“His spirit, just the way that he approaches the day, he’s a hell of a dude, he’s a hell of a competitor, one of the best at throwing the ball, honestly, and just his talent,” Prescott said.

“Just the way he’s jumped and progressed from year to year, I know what’s ahead of him.”

Another quarterback worth developing

The move gives Dallas three quarterbacks in the building with very different responsibilities.

Prescott remains firmly established as the starter after throwing for 4,552 yards and 30 touchdowns in 2025, earning the fourth Pro Bowl selection of his career.

Howell will serve as the immediate backup, while Milton gives Schottenheimer another developmental option who can continue learning without occupying a spot on the active roster. It also fits a broader theme around the Cowboys this offseason.

Dallas has operated with considerably less drama than in previous years, addressing contracts and roster decisions early enough to keep the conversation focused largely on football. Prescott has noticed the change.

“I think it not only allows us to be focused, but the narrative around us and the distraction or attention or whatever you want to say around us to be focused on just ball,” he said.

“We know what we’ve got. We know who we’ve got, and we’re ready to roll.”

Good feeling has an expiration date

The optimism is understandable after Dallas produced one of the NFL’s most productive offenses last season. The Cowboys finished second in total offense with 6,663 yards and scored 471 points.

George Pickens recorded 1,429 receiving yards, while CeeDee Lamb added another 1,077 as Prescott led a passing attack built to contend immediately. Still, Prescott isn't confusing a smooth offseason with actual progress.

“It’s definitely different,” he said. “I’m optimistic going into every season, it’s an NFL season, positive vibes and good energy doesn’t win you games.”

That's the standard facing Dallas as Prescott enters his 11th NFL season. Jones and Schottenheimer have created the quarterback room they wanted.

Prescott likes the direction. Now the Cowboys have to turn those decisions into wins. “We’ve got to go do it,” Prescott said. “We’ve got to go win games.”

articles.title: Cowboys legend Michael Irvin sparks wild controversy defending 49ers owner Jed York’s prostitution arrest
articles.standfirst: Michael Irvin comes to Jed York's defense after the 49ers owner's arrest.
articles.summary: Michael Irvin comes to Jed York's defense after the 49ers owner's arrest.
articles.body:
Pro Football Hall of Famer and three-time Super Bowl champion Michael Irvin has come to the defense of San Francisco 49ers owner Jed York following his recent arrest in Ohio during an undercover prostitution sting.

The legendary Dallas Cowboys wide receiver publicly backed York during a livestream with influencer Neon, downplaying the incident and urging people to stop turning it into a major scandal.

“(York) got divorced like 5-6 months ago,” Irvin said. “Is that really a crime? Let that man off. Leave that man alone. Imagine you’re going through a divorce and some young girl, some pretty girl, comes up to you, hitting on you, and she’s undercover … you don’t know. Everybody’s paying for it. You’re paying for it, regardless. Why do we gotta embarrass (York) over $140?”

According to authorities, York agreed to pay $140 to a sex worker he contacted online and was arrested while driving to a mobile home park where the meeting was allegedly set to take place.

Michael Irvin's controversial past

Irvin's remarks drew attention not only because he defended York, but also because of his own long history of off-field controversies throughout his playing career and retirement.

Much of that history is chronicled in Jeff Pearlman's Boys Will Be Boys: The Glory Days and Party Nights of the Dallas Cowboys Dynasty , as well as Netflix's 2025 documentary series America's Team: The Gambler And His Cowboys .

York, 46, became the 49ers' CEO in 2008 and has served as the franchise's principal owner since 2024. The York family controls more than 90 percent of the team and has an estimated net worth of $8.5 billion .

According to the San Francisco Chronicle , York used a fake name to arrange the meeting through text messages before driving to a mobile home park, believing he was headed to a one-hour sexual encounter in exchange for $140 .

When officers searched his vehicle, they found not only the cash intended for the encounter but also an additional, undisclosed amount of money in his wallet.

“He’s got all the money … he’s got a (expletive) load of money,” one officer says. “Wow. It’s crazy that people do this. They could do whatever they want. Like, they could do other things; they could go other ways. It’s wild.”

The Chronicle reported that York responded on Saturday to an advertisement posted on a prostitution website using the name “Joe.” After following up several times to arrange the meeting, an undercover officer eventually responded. The following day, York drove a rental car to the designated meeting spot in East Palestine, Ohio, carrying $160 in cash, where he was ultimately arrested by police.

articles.title: Dak Prescott more confident than ever he can end Dallas Cowboys trauma: "A lot of confidence"
articles.standfirst: The Cowboys quarterback is tired of hearing about three decades without a Super Bowl.
articles.summary: The Cowboys quarterback is tired of hearing about three decades without a Super Bowl.
articles.body:
Dak Prescott is entering another Dallas Cowboys season carrying the weight of one of the NFL's longest and most discussed droughts.

Dallas hasn't reached a Super Bowl since winning it all after the 1995 season, a reality Prescott knows follows the franchise into every new campaign.

This time, though, the quarterback isn't backing away from expectations. Instead, he says his belief in the Cowboys ' chances is stronger than ever.

"There's a lot of confidence," Prescott said.

That confidence comes despite another offseason in which Dallas' inability to turn regular season success into a deep playoff run has remained one of the biggest talking points around the team.

Dak Prescott frustrated by Cowboys' 30-year drought

Prescott has spent his entire NFL career trying to become the quarterback who finally changes that narrative.

He admitted the constant reminders of Dallas' championship drought aren't easy to hear.

"It pisses me off," Prescott said.

The Cowboys quarterback understands why the issue continues to dominate conversations around the franchise.

Dallas remains one of the most recognizable teams in American sports, and every season without a return to the Super Bowl adds another year to the pressure.

Prescott hasn't tried to distance himself from that responsibility.

Instead, he appears to be embracing it.

Prescott believes Cowboys can finally change the story

The quarterback's confidence is significant because Dallas enters the new season once again facing questions about whether this group can succeed when the stakes are highest.

Prescott has produced some of the best regular-season football of his career, but postseason disappointment has prevented the Cowboys from reaching the NFC Championship Game during his tenure.

That remains the standard against which he will ultimately be judged.

Prescott , however, isn't entering the season sounding defeated by the history surrounding him.

His frustration with the drought is matched by a belief that Dallas has what it needs to finally end it.

"There’s a lot of confidence," Prescott said.

After 30 years of waiting, Cowboys fans have heard optimism before.

Prescott now has another opportunity to turn those words into something Dallas has been chasing for three decades: a genuine Super Bowl run.

articles.title: Brian Schottenheimer is thrilled with Broderick Jones—and he’s rubbing it in the Steelers' faces
articles.standfirst: Jones gets a clean slate in Dallas after struggling to find consistency in Pittsburgh
articles.summary: Jones gets a clean slate in Dallas after struggling to find consistency in Pittsburgh
articles.body:
The Dallas Cowboys may have landed more than an offensive tackle when they acquired Broderick Jones from the Pittsburgh Steelers. They may have found a player who finally gets the stability and coaching environment he’s been looking for.

Jones arrived in Dallas following a surprising trade that sent him away from Pittsburgh after three seasons. The former first-round pick was selected 14th overall in 2023, but his time with the Steelers never developed as expected.

Injuries, inconsistent play and frequent movement between tackle positions made it difficult for him to establish himself.

Now, Cowboys head coach Brian Schottenheimer is sounding remarkably confident about what his new offensive tackle can become. His comments on Thursday even appeared to contain a subtle message for Jones ’ former team.

Schottenheimer praised Jones ’ athleticism, willingness to learn and ability to absorb coaching. At the same time, he revealed that Dallas is already working to change some of the techniques Jones was previously taught.

“Great job of learning the system,” Schottenheimer said. “Very athletic. Love how coachable he is. He would just eat up all the coaching they could give him. He’s doing terrific.

“There are some techniques he’s been taught that we’re having to retrain, and usually it takes a minute, but in terms of the athlete and young man, I’m sold.”

Dallas is giving Jones the stability he wanted

Perhaps the biggest difference is how the Cowboys intend to use him. Instead of continuing to move Jones between tackle spots, Schottenheimer has made it clear that the 25-year-old will focus on right tackle.

That could be especially important for Jones . During his time with the Steelers, he regularly bounced between the left and right sides of the offensive line.

Jones himself identified that constant movement as one of his biggest challenges, explaining that it made it difficult to get comfortable with his footwork and build chemistry with the teammates lining up beside him.

Dallas also isn’t treating Jones as simple insurance, as Schottenheimer has confirmed that he’ll compete directly with Terence Steele for the starting right tackle job. That gives Jones a legitimate opportunity to take control of a position rather than waiting for someone else’s injury to create an opening.

The move comes after a difficult 2025 season for Jones , which was cut short by a neck injury that required spinal fusion surgery. Pittsburgh later declined his fifth-year option before ultimately sending him to Dallas, adding another chapter to what’s been a disappointing start to his professional career.

There’s still plenty for Jones to prove. His performance in Pittsburgh didn’t consistently match the expectations attached to a former first-round selection, and his struggles in pass protection became a recurring concern.

However, the Cowboys clearly believe his physical talent is worth developing. Schottenheimer’s early enthusiasm suggests Dallas sees a player with tools that can still be unlocked.

If the Cowboys can correct Jones ’ technical flaws while allowing him to settle permanently on one side of the line, this trade could eventually look very different from Pittsburgh’s perspective.

articles.title: Jake Ferguson’s wife Haley Cavinder has perfect response to fan’s WAG criticism
articles.standfirst: The Cowboys tight end’s wife turned an awkward comment into a playful exchange on social media
articles.summary: The Cowboys tight end’s wife turned an awkward comment into a playful exchange on social media
articles.body:
Haley Cavinder has once again found herself at the center of an NFL conversation, but this time, she’s making it clear that she isn’t interested in taking the criticism too seriously.

The wife of Dallas Cowboys tight end Jake Ferguson recently shared a playful Instagram reel filmed at AT&T Stadium in Arlington, Texas.

Wearing Ferguson’s Cowboys jersey, black leggings and white shoes, Cavinder showed off her football skills while poking fun at one of the most debated labels attached to women connected to professional athletes.

In the caption, Cavinder wrote, “wt* is a WAG,” seemingly using the phrase sarcastically rather than embracing its traditional meaning. The abbreviation, which stands for wives and girlfriends of athletes, has become commonplace in sports culture.

However, it’s also sparked plenty of debate because some women associated with professional athletes feel the term reduces their identities to their relationships.

Cavinder’s post quickly attracted reactions from fans, including one person who questioned her financial motivations with the comment, “Someone who needs $$?” Rather than responding angrily, the social media personality appeared to brush off the remark with a sarcastic comeback.

“Ya let the girlies get their bag,” Cavinder replied.

Her response suggests that she wasn’t particularly bothered by the criticism and was instead willing to play along with the joke.

Cavinder isn’t the first high-profile NFL wife to discuss the controversial abbreviation. Claire Kittle , the wife of San Francisco 49ers star George Kittle , has previously shared a more nuanced view of the term.

During an appearance on the Up & Adams Show, Claire acknowledged that WAG is a convenient way of grouping together the wives and girlfriends of athletes. However, she also pointed out that the phrase has often been given a negative meaning and that women in these circles regularly face criticism.

Other NFL wives have been less comfortable with the label. Kylie Kelce, wife of former Philadelphia Eagles center Jason Kelce , has previously admitted that the term deeply bothered her. Kristin Juszczyk , wife of 49ers fullback Kyle Juszczyk , has also expressed frustration with the way the abbreviation is used.

The timing comes shortly after a major milestone in her personal life. Cavinder and Ferguson married at Miami’s Biltmore Hotel, following their relationship that began in September 2023. The couple became engaged in April 2025, and Ferguson’s former Cowboys teammate Will Grier reportedly officiated their wedding.

On the football field, Ferguson is also coming off an impressive season. He recorded 82 receptions for 600 yards and a career-best eight touchdowns before signing a four-year, $52 million contract extension with Dallas.

Cavinder , meanwhile, played college basketball at Fresno State and Miami before building a significant social media following. With careers and identities of their own, the couple appears more than comfortable handling the attention that comes with being part of the NFL spotlight.
