articles.title: Haley Cavinder reveals the secret to keeping Jake Ferguson from ordering takeout before the NFL season
articles.standfirst: The Cowboys tight end’s wife shared a funny moment at home as she prepares for her husband’s return to the field.
articles.summary: The Cowboys tight end’s wife shared a funny moment at home as she prepares for her husband’s return to the field.
articles.body:
H aley Cavinder found a peculiar way to keep Jake Ferguson away from one of his easiest options when mealtime arrives . The content creator shared a video from her kitchen showing her attempt to prepare a dish for her husband, after explaining that even learning how to properly wash a pan had become a challenge and that, if she could not figure it out, Jake might end up turning to takeout.

Haley Cavinder wanted to surprise him

Haley already knew what she wanted to cook, and Jake can even be heard in the background as she begins the recipe. However, the first problem came sooner than expected: she had not bought tostadas. To solve it, she turned to the tortillas she had at home and used them as a substitute . She then cooked the ground beef in the pan until it reached the consistency she wanted and continued with the next steps.

The situation became even funnier

Things got more complicated when Haley started worrying that everything might fall apart. Between last minute changes, ingredients that ended up in the trash and a few warnings to avoid getting burned, what seemed like a simple meal turned into a much bigger challenge than she had imagined .

What did Haley make for Jake Ferguson?

The mystery eventually had a very specific name: Crunchwrap Supremes. Haley decided to make the popular meal for her husband and took the process quite seriously, especially after remembering that Jake had previously told her the result was too salty.

This time, she decided to use roughly half the amount she had used before. Even while measuring the ingredients, she joked that it had to be done “with love,” making it clear that her goal was to create a version that would finally win the player over .

The beans could not be left out either. Haley mentioned that Jake likes them, so she added them while assembling the different layers. Then came one of the trickiest moments: closing everything without it falling apart. The tortilla started to open up, forcing her to adjust the preparation before continuing.

In the end, she managed to make a version she was happy with and that, at least from her perspective, looked much better. The video ended just when it seemed she had found the formula she was looking for and, with it, accomplished her goal: keeping Jake from ordering takeout .

Jake Ferguson prepares to return with the Cowboys

While Haley continues balancing her personal projects with her attempts to prepare a good meal for her husband, Jake is now just days away from beginning a new season with the Dallas Cowboys. The NFL regular season will begin on Wednesday, September 9, while Dallas will make its debut on Sunday, September 13, against the New York Giants .

Ferguson enters the new season after a preparation period that generated positive signs within the team. The tight end arrived at training camp healthy and stood out during practices for his ability to become an important option for Dak Prescott, particularly on intermediate routes and in the middle of the field.

His 2025 campaign had left some areas to improve. He finished with an average of 7.3 yards per reception and three fumbles, while also producing less after the catch . However, reports from this year’s camp highlighted a more explosive version of Ferguson, along with several eye catching plays.

Ferguson also remains an important part of Dallas’ offensive plans. Over his last three seasons, he has recorded 95 first downs , while his size, at 6-foot-5 and 250 pounds, makes him an especially useful target for Prescott.

At the beginning of September, the Cowboys even restructured his contract to create salary cap space, as the tight end gets closer to the moment that truly matters: returning to official game action.

articles.title: Cowboys get major George Pickens boost as receiver makes intentions clear
articles.standfirst: The Dallas star could be playing his way toward one of the biggest receiver contracts in football.
articles.summary: The Dallas star could be playing his way toward one of the biggest receiver contracts in football.
articles.body:
George Pickens enters the 2026 season with plenty at stake, but the Dallas Cowboys may ultimately benefit from exactly that.

Pickens is playing on the franchise tag worth around $27.3 million after Dallas decided not to negotiate a long-term deal before the deadline.

That leaves the 25-year-old with another season to prove his breakout 2025 campaign wasn't a one-off before potentially hitting the open market.

Bleacher Report's Kristopher Knox believes another big year could lead to a four-year, $142 million contract.

"Pickens is also still only 25 years old," Knox wrote.

George Pickens has huge contract motivation

Pickens produced the best season of his career in 2025, catching 93 passes for 1,429 yards and nine touchdowns during his first year with Dallas.

But Knox believes consistency will determine whether he reaches the very top of the receiver market.

"However, Pickens will need to show that he can consistently produce at a Pro Bowl level to earn a top-of-the-market deal," Knox wrote.

That gives Dallas a highly motivated receiver alongside CeeDee Lamb .

Pickens ' previous reputation will also remain part of the conversation after three inconsistent seasons with Pittsburgh and questions about his behavior.

"His production fluctuated during his three seasons with the Pittsburgh Steelers, and Pittsburgh was willing to trade him for third- and fifth-round picks last offseason," Knox wrote.

Cowboys could benefit before massive payday

The contract prediction is still only that, but another Pro Bowl-level season would put Pickens in an extremely strong position.

"Former Steelers head coach Mike Tomlin also questioned Pickens' ability to be a leader following the trade, which probably won't be forgotten by some team decision-makers," Knox wrote.

There is also a clear route to changing that perception.

"If Pickens has another Pro Bowl season while continuing to repair his locker-room reputation, he should be able to match recent receiver deals, like Drake London's four-year, $141.1 million extension, on the open market."

Pickens quickly signed his franchise tender in April, avoiding the kind of prolonged contract drama Dallas has dealt with before.

Now the equation is simple. If Pickens produces another elite season and keeps the focus on football, the Cowboys get another year of top-level production while he puts himself in position for a potentially enormous 2027 payday.

articles.title: Dallas Cowboys unite to silence Greg Newsome with CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens
articles.standfirst: Dallas has heard the challenge and believes its star receivers can provide the answer.
articles.summary: Dallas has heard the challenge and believes its star receivers can provide the answer.
articles.body:
The Dallas Cowboys have been handed some extra motivation before facing the New York Giants after cornerback Greg Newsome made a bold claim about how his secondary matches up with CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens .

Newsome didn't hide his confidence.

"I think we match up really well," he said.

The Giants cornerback believes New York has enough talent in the secondary to handle Dallas' two biggest receiving threats, but that message has only added fuel to a matchup already carrying plenty of attention.

Dallas enters the season with Lamb and Pickens forming one of the most dangerous receiver combinations in the NFC.

CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens give Cowboys their response

The Cowboys don't need to say much publicly when they can answer through their offense.

Lamb remains the centerpiece of Dallas' passing attack, while Pickens gives Dak Prescott another explosive option capable of stretching defenses and winning contested catches.

That combination is exactly why Newsome's confidence has attracted attention.

"I feel like our corners match up very well with their receivers," Newsome said.

The Giants clearly believe their defensive backs can make life difficult for Dallas.

articles.title: Dak Prescott and the Cowboys receive their first bad news of the 2026 season before it even begins
articles.standfirst: The Cowboys will kick off the season against the Giants in the first Sunday Night Football game
articles.summary: The Cowboys will kick off the season against the Giants in the first Sunday Night Football game
articles.body:
The NFL season starts this week, and one of the first confirmed marquee matchups of the year is the Sunday Night Football opener in Week 1, a classic NFC East clash featuring the Dallas Cowboys visiting the New York Giants .

This showdown marks the eighth time in 15 seasons that these fierce rivals have met in Week 1, showing the league's obsession with putting the Cowboys in primetime isn't accidental.

Over the last 17 seasons , the Cowboys have served as either the Kickoff Game or the SNF opener 12 times . In fact, they have opened the season in the standard 1 p.m. ET window just once in the last 25 years.

According to quarterback Dak Prescott , this year is strictly a Super Bowl-or-bust campaign in Dallas, despite a frustrating stretch that includes missing the playoffs for two consecutive seasons and a staggering 30-year drought since their last NFC Championship appearance.

Tough Medical Blow Shocks Dallas Ahead of Opener

Entering the season finale of preparations, the Cowboys looked to have navigated training camp and the preseason with a clean bill of health, but that reality shifted dramatically when head coach Brian Schottenheimer revealed that standout left guard Tyler Smith required immediate thumb surgery .

Smith attempted to play through the persistent issue, but with zero improvement, an operation became unavoidable. Consequently, the team is placing him on the injured reserve list with the designation to return, putting his recovery timeline at roughly four to six weeks .

Missing a premier lineman of Smith's caliber, who anchors the interior alongside center Cooper Beebe and right guard Tyler Booker , deals a heavy early-season setback to an offensive line that expected to be among the elite units in the league.

Next Man Up: Depth Tested in the NFC East

To absorb the loss of their star blocker, Dallas will pivot to reliable interior reserve T.J. Bass , who is slated to step into the starting lineup at left guard. Schottenheimer expressed confidence in the depth the front office has quietly cultivated, noting that Bass has logged significant snaps and valuable experience for the franchise.

Even with the upfront shuffle, the Cowboys still feature a formidable offensive arsenal; however, franchise leader Dak Prescott may need to release the football quicker while distributing targets to playmakers like CeeDee Lamb , George Pickens , and Javonte Williams .

Navigating this initial 4-to-6-week window without their best lineman will truly test whether Dallas has the roster depth required to conquer a fiercely competitive division from the jump

articles.title: How Joe Milton is coping after Cowboys crush his ambitions behind Dak Prescott and Sam Howell
articles.standfirst: Despite being released, Joe Milton III returned to Dallas with a clear message: he still believes he can become one of the NFL’s best quarterbacks.
articles.summary: Despite being released, Joe Milton III returned to Dallas with a clear message: he still believes he can become one of the NFL’s best quarterbacks.
articles.body:
The Dallas Cowboys will begin the 2026 season with Dak Prescott as their starting quarterback and Sam Howell as the top backup, but there is another signal-caller who has developed a special connection with the fan base: Joe Milton III .

The young quarterback, who is currently part of the practice squad, could not avoid being released last month despite his impressive arm strength and calm demeanor on the field. However, Dallas decided to give him another opportunity by bringing him back because of the potential they still see in his development.

Milton III explained that his return to the Cowboys was mainly driven by the trust he has built within the organization and the relationships he has developed with his teammates and coaches.

"Somewhat, but not really," Milton III said when asked if it was a difficult decision to rejoin the Cowboys after being waived. "I have a lot of relationships here and guys I trust with my development."

Despite the disappointment of being released, Milton said he has not lost confidence in his abilities and continues to maintain an ambitious mindset.

"I’m still the best quarterback in my eyes," Milton III said. "It is what it is. It’s something you got to live with and take to the chin."

Last season with Dallas, Milton III appeared in four games, throwing for 183 yards, one touchdown and two interceptions. Now, he will have the opportunity to continue developing behind Prescott and Howell, while receiving the support of the Cowboys' starting quarterback.

Dak Prescott has publicly shown his support for Milton’s return, and the young quarterback will look to make the most of this new opportunity as the Cowboys prepare for their season opener on September 13 against the New York Giants in East Rutherford, New Jersey.

articles.title: Tyler Smith's serious injury disrupts the Dallas Cowboys' plans for the start of the NFL season
articles.standfirst: Dallas must adjust its offensive line plans after Smith’s thumb injury
articles.summary: Dallas must adjust its offensive line plans after Smith’s thumb injury
articles.body:
The Dallas Cowboys have been handed an unwelcome setback just days before their 2026 season opener against the New York Giants , with All-Pro guard Tyler Smith set to miss four to six weeks after suffering a thumb injury.

Smith is scheduled to undergo surgery, creating an immediate hole in an offensive line that had been expected to provide stability from the opening snap.

Head coach Brian Schottenheimer explained that Smith had reached the point where playing through the problem wasn't the right option, particularly because grip strength is so important for an offensive lineman.

“At the end of the day, you always see if you can kinda play through these things,” Schottenheimer told reporters. “He’s done things like that, as a lot of guys have; they’ve been able to play through them.

“Unfortunately, when you’re an offensive lineman, grip strength and things like that are really important. Again, we know he’s a quick healer, and we want to get it fixed. He’ll be back before too long.”

Smith's absence is significant because he's developed into one of Dallas' most dependable offensive linemen since being selected 24th overall in the 2022 NFL Draft. After beginning his career at left tackle, he established himself as a force at left guard and earned Pro Bowl honors following the 2023, 2024 and 2025 seasons.

His previous injury problems have caused him to miss a handful of games, but none have created a situation quite like this so close to the beginning of a new season.

T.J. Bass gives Dallas a trusted replacement

Fortunately for the Cowboys, they aren't entering this crisis without an experienced option. T.J. Bass is expected to take over at left guard while Smith recovers, giving Dallas a player the coaching staff already knows and trusts.

Bass has appeared in 48 games during his three-year career and has made 10 starts. Five of those starts came during the 2025 season, meaning he's already demonstrated that he can handle an expanded role when circumstances demand it.

The Cowboys also made a significant commitment to keeping Bass this offseason, tendering him for approximately $5.76 million. That decision now looks particularly valuable.

It means that rather than having to search outside the organization for an emergency replacement, Dallas can turn to a lineman who's familiar with its system and has experience playing alongside key members of the current unit.

Schottenheimer has repeatedly expressed confidence in Bass , describing him as a talented player who's simply been stuck behind several highly regarded starters. Bass has previously played beside Cooper Beebe and Tyler Guyton , which should help minimize the disruption caused by Smith's absence.

There will inevitably be a difference between replacing an established All-Pro and inserting a reserve into the lineup. However, guard may be the position where Dallas is best equipped to absorb an injury of this magnitude.

The Cowboys will still need Bass to perform immediately, particularly with a demanding opening stretch ahead. But if he can provide dependable protection and maintain the physicality expected from Dallas' interior offensive line, the team should be able to weather Smith's absence.

articles.title: A fired FOX analyst's scathing criticism of Dallas Cowboys legend Troy Aikman's work at ESPN
articles.standfirst: Aikman’s legendary playing career may not be enough to convince everyone of his broadcasting talent
articles.summary: Aikman’s legendary playing career may not be enough to convince everyone of his broadcasting talent
articles.body:
Troy Aikman’s transition from Dallas Cowboys quarterback to one of football’s most recognizable broadcasters has lasted more than two decades, but his television work is now facing a fresh round of criticism.

Former FOX analyst LeSean McCoy offered a blunt assessment of Aikman during the September 7 episode of Speakeasy, saying he doesn’t believe the Hall of Famer is particularly impressive on television.

“I don’t think [Troy Aikman] is that great on TV,” said McCoy .

“I think he’s just cool. He just says what he sees. Nothing special. But when I look at his background check, I look at who he played with, when he played, the wins he had, the championships, the era with Jimmy Johnson, and all that, I would take him too.

“And you, with the brand of the cap, I would take you for that. It’s hard for me to push back because the resume checks the box.”

McCoy’s comments are notable because Aikman has spent years working at the highest level of NFL broadcasting and remains one of ESPN’s most prominent football voices.

That assessment is particularly striking given how quickly Aikman established himself after retiring. He joined FOX in 2001 and was eventually placed in the network’s top NFL booth, where he formed a hugely successful partnership with Joe Buck.

The duo spent two decades together before moving to ESPN in 2022 to become the voices of Monday Night Football.

Aikman’s résumé makes the criticism complicated

Aikman’s playing career gives him plenty of credibility when discussing the game. The Cowboys selected him first overall in 1989, and he spent all 12 NFL seasons in Dallas, winning three Super Bowls and earning Super Bowl XXVII MVP honors. He was inducted into the Pro Football Hall of Fame in 2006.

His statistics weren’t built around spectacular arm strength, but accuracy, timing and decision-making were central to his success. Aikman finished his career with 32,942 passing yards and 165 touchdowns while completing 61.5% of his passes. More importantly, he was the quarterback at the center of one of the NFL’s defining teams of the 1990s.

McCoy’s remarks also echo criticism from another outspoken media personality. Craig Carton previously called Aikman an “average quarterback,” arguing that his success was helped significantly by an elite supporting cast.

Carton pointed to the Cowboys’ dominant offensive line, Emmitt Smith, Michael Irvin and a strong defense as reasons Aikman’s legacy should be viewed differently.

That argument triggered plenty of backlash from fans, many of whom believe it overlooks Aikman’s ability to consistently deliver when the Cowboys were under enormous pressure. Winning three championships in four seasons remains difficult to dismiss, regardless of how talented the surrounding roster was.

McCoy’s latest criticism of Aikman is more about what makes an analyst compelling. ​ has experience, credibility and an established audience, but those qualities don’t guarantee that every viewer will consider his commentary exceptional.

For now, ESPN continues to trust him with one of the NFL’s most prestigious broadcast assignments. Aikman’s calm delivery and decades of football experience remain central to Monday Night Football.

articles.title: Dak Prescott leads the NFL in consecutive Week 1 starts closely followed by three AFC MVPs
articles.standfirst: Only 10 of the 32 quarterbacks have started with their current team for more than five seasons in Week 1
articles.summary: Only 10 of the 32 quarterbacks have started with their current team for more than five seasons in Week 1
articles.body:
The first game of the NFL season and Super Bowl rematch is around the corner with the Seattle Seahawks hosting the New England Patriots this Wednesday.

This year's kickoff change stems from a truly historic milestone as the NFL stages its very first regular-season game in Australia , featuring Super Bowl favorites the Los Angeles Rams squaring off against the San Francisco 49ers on Thursday Night Football, which is actually Friday local time in Australia.

For this season, almost a third (10) of teams will have a new head coach , and including the six coaches hired in 2025, half of the league now features leaders with less than two seasons at the helm .

Quarterback Continuity and Dak Prescott's Record Tenure in Dallas

Among quarterbacks, no rookies will start in Week 1 , but five teams will feature a new signal-caller to begin the season, including Malik Willis in Miami, Geno Smith with the Jets, Kirk Cousins in Las Vegas, Kyler Murray in Minnesota, and Tua Tagovailoa in Atlanta.

Furthermore, only 10 of the 32 starting quarterbacks in Week 1 have been with their current teams for more than five seasons, showing how fast the league moves without many noticing.

Take Dak Prescott , for instance, who will begin his 11th campaign as the starter, giving him the most consecutive seasons as a starter with the same franchise among active players.

At 33 years old, Dak is the sixth-oldest starting quarterback this year , a category led by Aaron Rodgers at 42 , yet he stands alone in longevity with his current club. His closest challenger in the NFC is Jalen Hurts , who is opening his seventh season as the Week 1 starter for the Philadelphia Eagles.

Following Prescott and Hurts are former 2021 trade acquisitions Matthew Stafford and Jared Goff , who embark on their sixth seasons as starters for the Rams and Lions, respectively, while Brock Purdy rounds out the top five with his fifth year, leaving all other NFC quarterbacks with less than half a decade of tenure in their current spots.

AFC Heavyweights Chasing Consistency Behind Established Veterans

Over in the AFC , the closest pursuers to Prescott's streak feature a powerhouse trio of former MVPs in Patrick Mahomes , Lamar Jackson , and Josh Allen , who are all starting their ninth consecutive seasons with their respective teams and enter as perennial favorites to reach the playoffs and contend for the Super Bowl .

Joe Burrow and Justin Herbert round out the top five in the conference alongside the elite group, entering their seventh seasons just like Jalen Hurts. While these veterans have occasionally drawn scrutiny in recent years, they anchor the conference's elite tier.

Every single year brings a flurry of roster moves at the game's most important position, so it remains to be seen how many of these signal-callers will extend their streaks next season, but for now, the best news of all is that football is back!

articles.title: 'Defense would be the spot': Jerry Jones hints at an imminent Cowboys trade before the clash against the Giants
articles.standfirst: Cowboys could turn their attention to defense after trading for Broderick Jones
articles.summary: Cowboys could turn their attention to defense after trading for Broderick Jones
articles.body:
Jerry Jones has once again opened the door to a potential Dallas Cowboys trade, and his latest comments suggest the defense would be the primary target. With the Cowboys preparing for their Week 1 matchup against the New York Giants, speculation surrounding the front office's plans has intensified.

The Cowboys have been connected to trade possibilities throughout the latter stages of the offseason, although no additional deal had materialized at the time of Jones ' comments.

Speaking on 105.3 The Fan, the Dallas owner and general manager explained that recent moves to create salary-cap flexibility have left the organization with enough financial room to pursue a deal if the right opportunity becomes available.

“That does show that we have really viable serious room financially to make trade if we wanted to right now,” said Jones .

Dallas created more than $19 million in additional cap space by restructuring the contracts of defensive tackle Kenny Clark , cornerback DaRon Bland and tight end Jake Ferguson . NFLPA figures have the Cowboys with approximately $33.6 million in available cap space, giving the franchise considerable flexibility as it begins the season.

Jones stressed that the additional room doesn't necessarily mean a trade is imminent. However, his comments confirmed that Dallas has the financial ability to make a move now rather than waiting until later in the campaign.

The most revealing part of his remarks concerned which side of the ball could receive another addition.

Why defense remains the Cowboys' biggest trade target

According to ESPN's Todd Archer, Jones indicated that the Cowboys would be more likely to pursue defensive help after addressing their offensive needs with the acquisition of Broderick Jones.

Dallas recently traded for the offensive tackle from the Pittsburgh Steelers, sending a third- and sixth-round pick to Pittsburgh in exchange for Jones and a fourth-round selection.

That move strengthens an offensive line that needed additional depth, while the Cowboys already appear comfortable with their skill-position groups. Jones has expressed confidence in the team's running backs, quarterback depth and tight ends, while CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens give Dallas a formidable receiving duo.

Defense, therefore, stands out as the most obvious area for improvement. The Cowboys struggled defensively last season, making reinforcements on that side of the ball a priority throughout the offseason.

Another addition could provide valuable depth while also giving the coaching staff greater flexibility as the season develops.

Dallas doesn't have to make a decision immediately. The NFL trade deadline is Nov. 10 at 4 p.m. ET, meaning the Cowboys have several weeks to assess their roster, injuries and performance before committing more draft capital.

The franchise currently owns first-, second-, fourth- and sixth-round selections in the 2027 draft. Jones has previously indicated that he'd be willing to use future draft capital if it meant substantially improving the team in 2026.

Defense, therefore, stands out as the most obvious area for improvement. The Cowboys struggled defensively last season, making reinforcements on that side of the ball a priority throughout the offseason.
Another addition could provide valuable depth while also giving the coaching staff greater flexibility as the season develops.

Dallas doesn't have to make a decision immediately. The NFL trade deadline is Nov. 10 at 4 p.m. ET, meaning the Cowboys have several weeks to assess their roster, injuries and performance before committing more draft capital.

The franchise currently owns first-, second-, fourth- and sixth-round selections in the 2027 draft. Jones has previously indicated that he'd be willing to use future draft capital if it meant substantially improving the team in 2026.

articles.title: Dak Prescott delivers defiant message as Dallas Cowboys star dismisses record obsession
articles.standfirst: Dak Prescott has broken plenty of records with the Cowboys, but the quarterback says there’s only one thing that will define his legacy.
articles.summary: Dak Prescott has broken plenty of records with the Cowboys, but the quarterback says there’s only one thing that will define his legacy.
articles.body:
It is no secret that Dak Prescott is used to breaking records with the Dallas Cowboys, although there remains a never-ending debt when it comes to winning a Super Bowl. Even so, the quarterback is very clear that individual accomplishments come second. Heading into the 2026 season , his main goal is simple: lead the franchise to win important games and compete for a championship once again.

Dak Prescott puts winning ahead of records

Prescott begins his journey toward his 11th season in the NFL as the Cowboys’ leader and arrives with the responsibility of guiding a team looking to move past the disappointment of recent years and return to the playoff race.

Although his career is already filled with historic milestones and individual accolades, the quarterback made it clear that those numbers are not the reason he plays. For Prescott, a true legacy is built through victories in the biggest moments.

“Records have never done it for me or excited me or been what I'm seeking out. Records are meant to be broken and I truly believe that. And so it's just my time to break these records. And yeah, to your point, I want to win the big game and that's my focus. That's what I care about. That's what I'll hang my head on when that happens,” Prescott said.

Cowboys confident in a revamped offense

After an offseason filled with adjustments, Dallas enters the new campaign with high expectations and the belief that its offense can become one of the most dangerous units in the league.

Prescott’s goal is for the Cowboys to have their best season in years, which would mean reaching the NFC Championship Game and, eventually, competing for a spot in the Super Bowl.

In 2025 , Prescott had one of the best seasons of his career, completing 404 passes for 4,552 yards, 30 touchdowns and 10 interceptions . He also contributed on the ground with 53 carries for 177 yards and two rushing touchdowns .

Now, Dallas will look to improve on its 7-9-1 record in 2025 and end a two-season playoff drought.

The Cowboys will open the season on the road against the New York Giants in Week 1, with the matchup scheduled for September 13 at 8:20 p.m. ET.

articles.title: Cowboys blockbuster coming? Jerry Jones keeps door wide open for pre-Week 1 trade
articles.standfirst: After a busy offseason, the Cowboys could still have another splashy move up their sleeve
articles.summary: After a busy offseason, the Cowboys could still have another splashy move up their sleeve
articles.body:
The Dallas Cowboys are heading into the 2026 season with plenty of intrigue, and owner Jerry Jones has added another layer by refusing to close the door on a potentially significant trade.

With Dallas preparing to face the New York Giants at MetLife Stadium in Week 1, Jones has made it clear that the Cowboys remain willing to explore a major deal if the right opportunity emerges.

The season opener is just around the corner, leaving Dallas with limited time to add another piece before the regular season gets underway.

Jones isn't promising that a blockbuster is imminent, as is position is considerably more measured. Dallas will make a move only if the circumstances line up and the addition genuinely improves the roster.

That distinction matters because the Cowboys have already shown they're willing to think big. Last year, Dallas traded Micah Parsons to the Green Bay Packers for a package headlined by two first-round picks and Kenny Clark .

The Cowboys later used some of that acquired draft capital to land Pro Bowl defensive tackle Quinnen Williams from the New York Jets.

Those moves demonstrated that Jones and the Cowboys' front office aren't necessarily afraid to make aggressive decisions when they believe a deal can significantly improve the team. The same approach could now apply as Dallas looks to build a defense capable of competing at the highest level.

Dallas still has room to make another splash

The possibility of another major addition isn't simply speculation, as Dallas has created additional financial flexibility by restructuring several contracts, giving the organization more room to maneuver if an appealing opportunity becomes available.

Jones has indicated that the Cowboys could use that flexibility to strengthen this year's roster, with another defensive addition appearing to be a particularly logical possibility.

Dallas has already undergone a significant defensive overhaul and brought in Christian Parker as defensive coordinator, so adding another proven playmaker could raise the unit's ceiling.

There may not be an obvious blockbuster available before Week 1, which makes an immediate deal difficult to predict. However, the trade landscape can change quickly once games begin. Players who appear unavailable now could become realistic targets if their teams struggle, injuries create roster needs or front offices change their plans.

Names such as Joey Porter Jr. have been floated as potential defensive targets, while other established pass rushers could become available if their respective teams reconsider their positions later in the season.

Jones is keeping his options open rather than forcing a deal. The Cowboys don't need to make a splash simply for the sake of making one, and Jones' comments suggest the team understands that.

Still, Dallas' recent willingness to make aggressive trades has changed the perception of the franchise. After years of conservative roster management, the Cowboys appear more prepared to use draft capital and financial flexibility if doing so gives them a better chance to compete for a championship.

If the right opportunity appears before or after Week 1, don't be surprised if Jones picks up the phone.

articles.title: Brian Burns is clear about the Cowboys' weak point: "It's an opportunity to take advantage of it"
articles.standfirst: Star showdown in this Sunday's NFL slate
articles.summary: Star showdown in this Sunday's NFL slate
articles.body:
John Harbaugh's New York Giants know how to hurt the Dallas Cowboys in their Sunday Night Football matchup in Week 1 of the NFL season.

At least that's what Brian Burns claims, who exposed a weakness in Brian Schottenheimer's team ahead of the game. The Giants defender believes the Cowboys are weak at right tackle with Broderick Jones and Terence Steele.

“I mean, the opportunity is within the game. They’re both professionals. Without disrespecting anyone’s profession or anything like that, the fact that they’re so concerned in that aspect does alert us, I suppose, knowing that they’re having difficulties. … So we can definitely see it as an opportunity to take advantage of it,” he told the New York Daily News.

Harbaugh doesn't want to "screw it up"

For his part, the Giants' coach expressed his feelings before his debut with his new team. “In my first game in Baltimore, the first thing I thought was: ‘Hey, don’t screw it up.’ And that could be my first thought in this game too: trying not to mess it up,” he confessed.

"Probably what everyone thinks. You want to have more positives than negatives. But besides that, it will be a great moment to enjoy," he explained. Regarding the tributes for the 9/11 anniversary, he was also clear: "I don't think it's going to be a problem, I don't think I'm going to lose control and start crying on the sideline or anything like that. I think it's going to be meaningful," he stated.

articles.title: Cowboys vs Giants: Where to watch Dak Prescott's with Dallas and what is today's game kickoff time
articles.standfirst: The Cowboys visit MetLife to open the season: Prescott and company, favorites against a Giants team led by Jaxson Dart
articles.summary: The Cowboys visit MetLife to open the season: Prescott and company, favorites against a Giants team led by Jaxson Dart
articles.body:
The NFL kicks off this weekend, and it does so with one of the marquee matchups on the schedule: the oldest and fiercest rivalry in the NFC East . The New York Giants host the Dallas Cowboys in a divisional showdown that always goes beyond the scoreline, and this year it arrives loaded with intrigue because of what it represents for both locker rooms.

Here we tell you the schedule, where to watch it, and everything that's at stake.

What time does the Cowboys game start and where to watch it?

The NFC East matchup will take place this Sunday, September 13 at MetLife Stadium in East Rutherford, which has a capacity of 82,500 fans. The game time corresponds to the Sunday Night Football primetime slot:

Sunday night matchups are NBC's usual territory, so that's the right place to point the remote to watch the game between Dallas and New York; meanwhile, via streaming, the game can be followed on Peacock.

What team is favored to win? Cowboys vs Giants prediction and picks

There is no better way to kick off a season than with an NFC East clash. It’s the kind of game where history, pride, and the divisional weight matter just as much as the talent on the gridiron. Both teams begin with a 0-0 record, like the rest of the league at the start, but the market is already showing a clear difference.

The Cowboys come in as favorites : the sportsbook gives them an implied 58.7% chance of taking the win, compared to the Giants' 41.3%. In the point spread market, Dallas appears as a favorite by between 2.5 and 3.5 points, while the total points line (over/under) sits around 48 points, a sign that the market anticipates a game with offenses capable of putting points on the board.

The market isn’t wrong to tip the scales toward Dallas, and everything points to a high-scoring game with two offenses capable of putting up points on any possession. The experience of Dak Prescott and the Lamb–Pickens duo gives the Cowboys a real edge against a Giants team debuting a new quarterback on the biggest stage.

Logic says Dallas by a narrow margin, close to the 3-point spread; but if Jaxson Dart rises to the occasion and Malik Nabers finds his space, MetLife could witness a massive surprise in the season opener.

Implications for the NFC East

In the NFC East there is no room for stumbles, especially not in Week 1. A win for the Cowboys would give them a morale boost and an early divisional advantage over a direct rival in their own home.

For the Giants , meanwhile, winning in Jaxson Dart 's debut would be the perfect statement of intent to kick off a project that aims to bring the franchise back into the playoff conversation.

Each victory within the division counts double when it comes to end-of-season tiebreakers, and that is why this first chapter carries weight that goes beyond the date.

The star matchup between rosters: two offenses with marquee names

The big story on the New York side is the start of a new era under the command of Jaxson Dart, the 23-year-old young quarterback who tops the depth chart ahead of veteran Jameis Winston.

Dart has at his disposal one of the most eye-catching receiving arsenals in the league: rising star Malik Nabers, wearing No. 1, will be his primary target, with the experienced Odell Beckham Jr. and Darnell Mooney rounding out the receiving corps.

In the backfield, the Giants opted for depth with Cameron Skattebo , veteran Najee Harris and Devin Singletary, while the offensive line relies on the solid tackle Andrew Thomas.

On Dallas' side, the constant remains Dak Prescott, the 33-year-old quarterback who leads the Cowboys' offense. His most dangerous connection is with star wide receiver CeeDee Lamb , who wears the iconic 88, now joined by George Pickens , an addition that gives Prescott two top-level vertical threats.

The explosive KaVontae Turpin brings speed as a receiver and on special teams, while Javonte Williams leads the ground attack. Tight end Jake Ferguson rounds out a group of weapons that makes this offense one of the most feared in the conference. Up front, he is protected by a line featuring Tyler Smith , one of the NFL’s most highly regarded guards.

articles.title: Jerry Jones drops wild declaration on player destined to alter Cowboys' destiny
articles.standfirst: Jerry Jones makes a shocking prediction about the Cowboys rookie who could change the franchise’s future.
articles.summary: Jerry Jones makes a shocking prediction about the Cowboys rookie who could change the franchise’s future.
articles.body:
The Dallas Cowboys are ready to open the season against the New York Giants in Week 1 of the NFL, and after an offseason focused on rebuilding their defense, team owner Jerry Jones has high expectations for his squad. In particular, he has complete confidence in Caleb Downs , the team’s first-round draft pick.

Ahead of the highly anticipated Sunday Night Football matchup, Jones said the young defender is ready to make the jump to the NFL and will not allow the pressure of his debut to impact his performance, according to Joseph Hoyt of The Dallas Morning News .

“It won't be too big for him,” Jones said about Downs. “He's got his head on straight. He'll be able to come out and compete without worrying about first-time jitters in the NFL. We're really proud to have him.”

The Cowboys selected Downs with the No. 11 overall pick in the Draft , making him one of the franchise’s biggest bets to transform a defense that struggled last season. The former Ohio State standout will begin his career as a nickel cornerback, a position that head coach Brian Schottenheimer believes will accelerate his development and allow him to quickly become a key piece of the secondary.

Downs arrives in Dallas with an impressive college résumé. He began his career with the Alabama Crimson Tide as a freshman before transferring to Ohio State to play under Ryan Day . Over three seasons, he appeared in 44 games, recording 257 tackles (164 solo), 1.5 sacks, six interceptions, three forced fumbles, and one fumble recovery.

The defensive back was one of Jerry Jones’ biggest offseason additions to a Cowboys defense that also added talent and experience with pass rushers R ashan Gary and Von Miller, looking to elevate a unit that needs to regain its dominance.

With the performance he showed at the college level, Caleb Downs has the opportunity to become one of the NFL’s most impactful rookies and one of the foundational pieces of the Cowboys’ new defensive project.

articles.title: Dallas Cowboys’ defense completely collapses in painful loss as fans demand answers
articles.standfirst: The Cowboys promised a defensive revival. Instead, Week 1 exposed the same problems that haunted them last season.
articles.summary: The Cowboys promised a defensive revival. Instead, Week 1 exposed the same problems that haunted them last season.
articles.body:
The Dallas Cowboys ’ debut in the 2026 NFL season left more questions than answers, especially on a defense that was expected to take a major step forward. The new defense designed by coordinator Christian Parker was exposed for much of the game by the New York Giants and young quarterback Jaxson Dart , once again raising concerns about a unit that was expected to undergo a major transformation.

During the offseason, Dallas had generated optimism after a previous campaign defined by defensive struggles under Matt Eberflus , when the team allowed 511 points , the highest total in the entire league. The expectation was that the adjustments, new additions, and the return of key players like DeRon Bland, Shavon Revel, and DeMarvion Overshown would help spark a defensive resurgence.

But the reality in Week 1 was completely different. The Giants imposed their will and built a 28-14 lead with just over seven minutes remaining, while also dominating possession by controlling the clock for 31 of the 52 minutes played .

As if the loss wasn’t enough, Dallas suffered another major blow with DeMarvion Overshown’s injury . The linebacker, who entered the season expected to become one of the leaders of the defense in the final year of his contract, left the game during the fourth quarter after suffering a hamstring injury.

DeMarvion Overshown raises concerns for the Cowboys

Several reporters covering the Cowboys reported that Overshown was listed as questionable to return to the game.

Jon Machota of The Athletic explained the play where the injury occurred:

“DeMarvion Overshown tripped on the previous play and immediately grabbed the back of his right leg. He’s questionable with a hamstring injury. It looks like his night could be done.”

The situation represents a major problem for Dallas, as one of the defense’s biggest concerns was precisely the lack of depth at linebacker. Overshown and Dee Winters were the starters, and the former’s absence forced third-round rookie Jaishawn Barham into an unexpected role.

Overshown was also responsible for wearing the defensive communication device known as the “green dot,” a key responsibility for organizing the unit on the field.

The Dallas Cowboys ultimately lost 28-20 to the New York Giants, with no clear signs of defensive improvement. Now, they will hope things improve in their second divisional matchup against the Washington Commanders.

articles.title: Haley Cavinder joined Jake Ferguson and ended up witnessing the same Cowboys nightmare
articles.standfirst: Jake Ferguson’s wife turned heads with a look made just for him, but the Cowboys’ first game ended far from the celebration she had imagined.
articles.summary: Jake Ferguson’s wife turned heads with a look made just for him, but the Cowboys’ first game ended far from the celebration she had imagined.
articles.body:
H aley Cavinder didn’t need to say a word to make it clear who she had come to support. For the Dallas Cowboys’ first game of the 2026 season, Jake Ferguson’s wife showed up at MetLife Stadium in a look that had her husband’s name practically everywhere. Everything was set for an NFL afternoon that, at least from the stands, had plenty of reasons to feel like a celebration.

The look that said “Mrs. Fergy” without needing an explanation

The base of the outfit looked simple: a white top with the phrase “I Cowboys” across the front and denim jeans. But once she turned around, the outfit completely changed.

The back of the top featured No. 87 and the last name “FERGUSON,” while the jeans had an even more personal detail: “MRS. Fergy” written across the back, along with a white textured detail near the bottom of the pants.

For Jake Ferguson, the season was starting with something different

The game also carried a particular meaning for Ferguson after everything that had happened off the field over the summer.

The Dallas tight end married Haley on June 20, 2026, in a wedding held in Miami at the Biltmore Hotel . Now, just a few weeks later, the two were sharing another important moment, although this time inside an NFL stadium with Ferguson beginning a new season with the Cowboys.

On the football side, expectations around him were also high. Ferguson was coming off what had been considered his best season and had earned his second Pro Bowl , in addition to signing a contract extension. He had also become one of Dak Prescott’s trusted options, especially near the goal line.

That gave Haley’s presence an extra layer: she wasn’t simply there to watch her husband play. She was there to see him begin another season with the expectation that he could take another step forward.

Dallas entered as the favorite… and that’s when everything started to get complicated

The Cowboys weren’t heading into their matchup against the New York Giants like just any team, either.

articles.title: "We haven't been up to par": Brian Schottenheimer blasts Cowboys' "unacceptable" execution after Week 1 disaster
articles.standfirst: Dallas' highly anticipated 2026 overhaul got off to a miserable start as the Cowboys fell 28-20 to the New York Giants
articles.summary: Dallas' highly anticipated 2026 overhaul got off to a miserable start as the Cowboys fell 28-20 to the New York Giants
articles.body:
The Dallas Cowboys entered their 2026 season opener expecting a fresh start. Instead, their first game under a heavily revamped defense exposed many of the same issues that had plagued the team previously.

A 28-20 defeat to the New York Giants at MetLife Stadium left head coach Brian Schottenheimer openly frustrated with the Cowboys ' execution, as Dallas struggled to establish the run, contain New York's rushing attack and avoid costly mistakes.

The loss also gave new Giants head coach John Harbaugh a victory in his first regular-season game with the franchise.

Schottenheimer did not attempt to disguise his frustration with the performance.

"Not good enough on either side of the ball. We gotta do a better job running the ball, stopping the run. The penalties aren’t good enough. Too many drops. We’ll get going. A lot of things to clean up," Brian said, according to The Athletic reporter Jon Machota .

That assessment summed up a night in which Dallas repeatedly made life harder for itself. The Cowboys were penalized heavily early, while their offense struggled to find consistency against a Giants defense that generated pressure without needing to rely on aggressive blitz packages.

The problems were particularly concerning because expectations had been raised considerably during the offseason.

Dallas had made significant changes to its defense after a poor 2025 campaign, appointing Christian Parker as defensive coordinator and adding new personnel in an effort to create a more aggressive and reliable unit. NFL.com had identified the revamped defense as one of the central storylines heading into the opener.

Instead, Jaxson Dart and the Giants offense controlled long stretches of the game. Dart completed 23 of 29 passes for 230 yards and three touchdowns while adding 54 rushing yards, while New York finished with 165 rushing yards and controlled possession for more than 36 minutes.

Dallas also had problems protecting Dak Prescott . The quarterback finished the game with 175 passing yards, two touchdowns and an interception, with the Giants repeatedly creating pressure with their front four.

Cowboys' biggest concerns go far beyond one bad night

One of the clearest problems entering the game was the condition of Dallas' offensive line. Three-time Pro Bowl guard Tyler Smith had been placed on injured reserve after thumb surgery, forcing T.J. Bass into the starting lineup. NFL.com had already highlighted Smith's absence as a major concern before kickoff.

The Giants were more than willing to test that weakness. Brian Burns had already suggested that Dallas' situation at right tackle could provide an opening for New York's pass rush.

"Not to disrespect anybody’s craft or anything like that," Burns said via Pat Leonard of the New York Daily News.

"But the fact that they are so concerned in that area does, I guess, raise some form of an alert in our minds, as far as like just knowing that they’re having struggles. . . . So we can definitely see that as an opportunity to exploit."

New York did precisely that, with Burns and Kayvon Thibodeaux helping create pressure that prevented Prescott from consistently settling into the pocket.

The struggles also prevented Dallas' expensive-looking receiver combination from taking over. George Pickens had entered the season alongside CeeDee Lamb with enormous expectations and had previously declared: "Yeah, we definitely think we’re the best."

The Giants did not allow the pair to dominate. Lamb did score a touchdown, but Dallas' passing game lacked the explosiveness expected from the new-look offense.

Pickens was particularly frustrated by dropped opportunities, including a deep Prescott pass that went through his hands on a potentially important drive.

The result was a statistical performance that fell well short of the Cowboys ' expectations.

Defensively, the concerns were just as significant. Christian Parker 's first game in charge of the Dallas defense ended with the Giants scoring 28 points and consistently sustaining drives.

Isaiah Likely was particularly damaging, catching eight passes for 78 yards and two touchdowns, while Skattebo added a rushing score.

Schottenheimer therefore has plenty to address before Dallas returns to action. The Cowboys were not simply beaten by a handful of spectacular plays; they were repeatedly undone by penalties, missed opportunities, poor execution and an inability to control the line of scrimmage.

The encouraging part for Dallas is that this was only Week 1. The season is long enough for Parker's defense to develop, the offensive line to adjust and Prescott's supporting cast to find its rhythm.

But the standard is considerably higher in Dallas, and Schottenheimer knows it.

After an offseason built around fixing the problems that contributed to last year's disappointment, the Cowboys delivered an opening performance that suggested the work is far from finished.

articles.title: Stephen A. Smith brutally mocks the Cowboys' collapse: "How many times do I have to be right?"
articles.standfirst: The ESPN personality wasted no time revisiting his long-running criticism of Dallas after the Cowboys were beaten 28-20 by the New York Giants in Week 1
articles.summary: The ESPN personality wasted no time revisiting his long-running criticism of Dallas after the Cowboys were beaten 28-20 by the New York Giants in Week 1
articles.body:
S tephen A. Smith did not need much of an invitation to revisit his long-running skepticism about the Dallas Cowboys .

After Dallas opened the 2026 NFL season with a 28-20 defeat to the New York Giants on Sunday Night Football, the ESPN personality once again had an opportunity to remind Cowboys fans of the concerns he has raised about the franchise for years.

Smith has made his criticism of America's Team one of the most recognizable parts of his television persona. Whenever Dallas suffers another high-profile setback, the ESPN commentator is usually among the first to point back to his previous warnings.

This time, Smith's reaction centered on the familiar argument that Cowboys supporters have repeatedly been told to remain patient.

"How many times will I be right?" Smith said. "How many times I'm not gonna be right? 'Just be patient, they won't let you down.'"

The comments came after the Cowboys were unable to overcome a fast start from the Giants , who controlled much of the game and handed Dallas an early divisional defeat.

New York produced 394 total yards and held possession for more than 36 minutes. Second-year quarterback Jaxson Dart completed 23 of 29 passes for 230 yards and three touchdowns while also contributing 54 rushing yards.

The Giants ' running game added another 165 yards as New York repeatedly kept the Cowboys ' defense on the field.

For Dallas, Dak Prescott finished with 175 passing yards and two touchdown passes, but he also threw an interception. The Cowboys struggled to sustain drives consistently and were unable to prevent the Giants from controlling the tempo.

Stephen A. Smith gets another opportunity to question the Cowboys

The result was particularly significant because Dallas entered the season hoping that a new campaign would produce a different story.

The Cowboys finished 7-9-1 in 2025 and have spent the offseason attempting to address weaknesses that have repeatedly prevented them from meeting expectations. Yet their first game of 2026 immediately brought back some of the same questions.

Head coach Brian Schottenheimer was blunt when assessing his team's performance afterward, acknowledging that Dallas had been outplayed and "humbled" by the Giants. That assessment reflected the statistical reality of the game.

New York converted nine of 11 third-down opportunities, allowing the Giants to extend drives and maintain control. Dallas also struggled to establish enough consistency on offense to force the Giants into uncomfortable situations.

Cam Skattebo was another major factor. The running back, returning from the serious ankle injury he suffered last season, rushed for 81 yards and a touchdown. His performance provided another example of the Giants ' ability to generate production when it mattered.

The Giants also received an important contribution from Malik Nabers , who returned from the knee injuries that ended his 2025 season. Nabers finished with six receptions for 69 yards, while tight end Isaiah Likely caught eight passes for 78 yards and two touchdowns.

For Smith , however, the individual statistics are secondary to the larger point he has made about Dallas.

His criticism has generally focused less on whether the Cowboys possess talented players and more on whether the organization can consistently turn that talent into results. The Week 1 defeat gave him another opportunity to argue that preseason optimism means little if the team cannot execute once the games begin.

There is, of course, a long way to go. One defeat does not determine an NFL season, and Dallas has plenty of opportunities to respond. The Cowboys will also have opportunities to correct the mistakes that contributed to Sunday's loss.

But the manner of the defeat made it particularly difficult for the organization to dismiss the criticism.

The Giants dictated possession, won important third-down situations and produced three passing touchdowns from Dart. Dallas, meanwhile, struggled to find answers once New York established control.

That is precisely why Smith's comments are likely to resonate with Cowboys fans — whether they agree with him or not.

For supporters, the hope is that Week 1 represents an early stumble rather than another chapter in a familiar story. For Smith , it represents something very different: another chance to ask why the Cowboys continue to disappoint when expectations rise.

And after another nationally televised Dallas defeat, he was ready with his answer.

articles.title: "They don't deserve to eat": Cowboys heavily criticized for ordering a lavish banquet after the loss to the Giants
articles.standfirst: Schottenheimer’s young defense excuses fall flat after Giants dominate
articles.summary: Schottenheimer’s young defense excuses fall flat after Giants dominate
articles.body:
After opening the 2026 NFL season with a frustrating 28-20 loss to the rival New York Giants , the Dallas Cowboys managed to infuriate their fan base before even boarding their flight home.

Instead of reflecting on an uninspired performance, the team treated itself to a massive, catered postgame feast from Katz's Deli, complete with a lavish spread set up right in the stadium hallway.

Longtime beat reporter Clarence Hill Jr. shared photos of the feast online, sparking immediate backlash from fans and analysts who voiced serious concerns about the organization's current culture and total lack of accountability.

Hill aptly noted that legendary former coach Jimmy Johnson would've knocked the entire buffet over in anger. The incident underscored a massive divide between today's comfortable Cowboys standards and the unforgiving expectations of the 1990s dynasty.

Johnson’s grueling practices built back-to-back Super Bowl champions who hated losing more than they loved winning. Following tough defeats, Johnson famously instructed flight attendants to withhold all postgame plane meals, bluntly stating his players didn't deserve to eat if they didn't feel physically sick to their stomachs after a loss.

Former defensive star Tony Casillas admitted Johnson operated like a dictator, yet acknowledged that his relentless focus on discipline was precisely what enabled that era's roster to reach its full potential.

“At times Jimmy was crazy as far as the way he motivated people and players, and you look back, like, how did I survive that? That was a form of abuse,” Casillas said on the Sunset Loung DFW podcast.

Defense collapses while Schottenheimer struggles for answers

The hallway buffet looked especially egregious considering the defensive catastrophe that unfolded on the field.

Despite glowing offseason praise from owner Jerry Jones and star quarterback Dak Prescott , the team's revamped defense collapsed under pressure. New York head coach John Harbaugh unveiled a physical "bully football" strategy that completely dominated the line of scrimmage.

Giants quarterback Jaxson Dart carved up the Dallas secondary for 230 passing yards and three touchdowns while adding 54 rushing yards.

Running back Cam Skattebo added 81 yards on the ground, allowing New York to convert 9 of 11 third downs with ease. Even with dynamic weapons like CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens on offense, Dallas couldn't maintain enough rhythm to offset its defensive breakdowns.

Head coach Brian Schottenheimer offered little comfort during his postgame press conference. While insisting he wasn't offering excuses, he repeatedly pointed to young defenders blowing basic containment assignments and missing coverage responsibilities in the flat.

“Those are going to happen, and we have to coach the young players better. But when you play young players, it’s part of the deal, and they need to learn quickly,” said Schottenheimer .

Critics quickly challenged that narrative, pointing out that the defense wasn't composed solely of rookies; it featured numerous high-priced veterans who didn’t perform.

Defensive coordinator Christian Parker endured a nightmare play-calling debut, leaving his unit looking undisciplined and unprepared.

With another high-stakes division matchup coming up at AT&T Stadium, the Cowboys don't have time to wonder about where things went wrong. They must address their glaring schematic issues and rediscover their competitive edge before their season gets derailed.

articles.title: The Cowboys Are Already Paying the Price for a Preseason Decision After Losing to the Giants
articles.standfirst: The lack of playing time for their starters raises a question: Did protecting a defense that was completely rebuilt in August leave it unprepared for September?
articles.summary: La falta de rodaje de sus titulares abre un interrogante ¿Proteger una defensa completamente reconstruida en agosto la dejó poco preparada para septiembre?
articles.body:
D Dallas lost 28-20 to the Giants in the season opener and gave up 394 yards. Christian Parker's new unit went into the first game without having played a single preseason game with its starters on the field.

América's team wrapped up its preseason by rebuilding a defense that desperately needed a fresh start, and expectations were high.

The Giants found too many open spaces

This Sunday night, the Cowboys finally showed the results of their strategy.

The Cowboys were unable to start the season with a win. The 28-20 loss to the Giants also exposed several defensive issues that Dallas will need to address quickly: New York gained 394 yards, dominated possession, and found ways to score both on the ground and through the air.

A decision made during the offseason now seems more interesting. The Cowboys did not play their projected defensive starters together during the preseason. Christian Parker took over as coordinator, and Dallas added several new players. However, the starters barely played any minutes together during the preseason—a decision intended to protect them from potential injuries.

The reason was understandable. Dallas wanted to avoid unnecessary injuries and believed that joint practices and training camp provided sufficient preparation.

That lack of experience in actual games seemed to be a factor against New York. The Giants rushed for 165 yards, quarterback Jaxson Dart completed 23 of 29 passes for 230 yards and three touchdowns, and Dallas struggled to get off the field. New York converted an extraordinary 9 of 10 third downs.

That dominance was reflected in their possession of the ball. The Giants had the ball for more than 36 minutes and forced Dallas to defend for long drives . On third downs, New York also converted nine of its ten attempts.

For a defense that is still learning a new system, the lack of collective playing time can become a problem. The Cowboys held practices over the summer, but the demands of an official game are different, and the first test revealed several visible issues that the coaching staff and players need to address.

Brian Schottenheimer acknowledged that his team was outmatched physically by the Giants . The coach will also need to analyze why a defense that had undergone so many changes was unable to contain New York's offense during the early stages of the game.

It is still too early to determine whether the decision to rest the starters during the preseason had any real negative impact. The season has just begun, and the defense will have time to improve its coordination.

But the first game revealed a statistic that’s hard to ignore: 394 yards allowed. Against Washington, Dallas will have its first chance to prove that the problems in its season opener were just a one-time occurrence and not a sign of a deeper weakness.

Brian Schottenheimer acknowledged that his team was outmatched physically by the Giants . The coach will also need to analyze why a defense that had undergone so many changes was unable to contain New York's offense during the early stages of the game.

It is still too early to determine whether the decision to rest the starters during the preseason had any real negative impact. The season has just begun, and the defense will have time to improve its coordination.

articles.title: A bad game, even worse news: Two Cowboys starters are out with injuries after the Week 1 disaster
articles.standfirst: Dallas' defensive woes deepen with concerning injuries to two starters
articles.summary: Dallas' defensive woes deepen with concerning injuries to two starters
articles.body:
The Dallas Cowboys couldn't have asked for a much rougher opening to the new NFL season. Dallas suffered a 28-20 loss to the New York Giants on Sunday, and the disappointing result was made even worse by injury concerns involving two defensive starters.

Dak Prescott finished the game 22-of-34 passing for 175 yards, two touchdowns and one interception while also adding 14 yards on two carries.

Running back Javonte Williams provided one of the few bright spots for Dallas, rushing for 41 yards on 12 attempts while scoring a touchdown. He also contributed five receptions for 31 yards and another score.

Those individual performances weren't enough to prevent Dallas from beginning the season with a loss to a division rival. The Cowboys' defensive struggles were especially concerning, and the situation became more complicated when injuries forced two key players out of the contest.

Malik Hooker was the first major concern. The veteran safety left the game late in the third quarter after suffering a forearm injury and wasn't able to return. He finished the night with one solo tackle.

Head coach Brian Schottenheimer provided an unsettling update after the game, saying Hooker might have fractured his forearm. The veteran will need further evaluation to determine the full extent of the injury, but a fracture would likely mean an extended absence.

Given the Dallas defense already had plenty to answer for after surrendering 28 points, losing an experienced safety could create another significant challenge.

Cowboys' defensive depth faces an early test

The injury situation became even more concerning when linebacker DeMarvion Overshown was forced out in the fourth quarter with a hamstring problem.

Overshown appeared to suffer the injury after tripping over a Giants player during a running play. Although he was able to leave the field under his own power, he didn't return to the game.

Schottenheimer said after the contest that the Cowboys didn't yet know the severity of Overshown's injury. The linebacker was expected to undergo additional testing Monday, which should provide a clearer picture of whether he'll be available for Week 2 or could face a longer absence.

That's particularly significant because Overshown has already dealt with serious injuries during his career. If he misses time, Dallas could be forced to rely more heavily on its younger linebackers. Rookie Jaishawn Barham could see his responsibilities increase, while Shemar James could also receive additional defensive snaps.

The Cowboys could also explore outside options if Overshown's injury proves serious. Dallas has players such as Justin Barron and Curtis Robinson available for depth, but the team could consider the trade or free-agent markets if it believes another experienced linebacker is needed.

The same applies to the safety position. If Hooker is sidelined, P.J. Locke could be asked to fill his role, while Markquese Bell or Alijah Clark could see increased opportunities.

Dallas has to wait for more definitive medical information. The Cowboys will host the Washington Commanders in Week 2, with kickoff scheduled for 4:25 p.m. ET on Sept. 20.

After an ugly season opener, Dallas desperately needs a response. Before that can happen, though, the Cowboys need to know exactly how much their defense has been weakened by Sunday's injuries.

articles.title: The rise of non-alcoholic beer in the U.S. brings together two NFL stars
articles.standfirst: Drake Maye and Dak Prescott join the company specializing in this beverage, Athletic Brewing Company, as athlete-owners
articles.summary: Drake Maye and Dak Prescott join the company specializing in this beverage, Athletic Brewing Company, as athlete-owners
articles.body:
"A thletic Brewing Company , the American brewery exclusively dedicated to non-alcoholic beverages, announced a few days ago a multi-year partnership with two of the NFL’s star quarterbacks , Drake Maye and Dak Prescott. This partnership goes a bit further, as both have joined as what they call ‘athlete-owners’ and will participate in exclusive marketing campaigns for the brand.

Athletic is an increasingly established brand and is leveraging sports to reach the public. It maintains major partnerships in the world of professional American football, football, baseball, lacrosse, hockey, college sports… The brand is already present in many sports venues.

There is no doubt that both Prescott and Maye are betting big on the rise of non-alcoholic beer across the United States. In 2026, the global market for this beverage was valued at between $26.2 billion and $28.62 billion. In fact, a study published 12 months ago by Gallup (an American analytics, management consulting, and public opinion polling company), concluded that the percentage of American adults who say they drink alcohol has fallen to 54% .

This is the lowest percentage in almost 90 years , and Gallup has been tracking Americans' alcohol consumption habits since 1939 and knows market trends perfectly well. According to its study, the decline in alcohol consumption in recent years is notable.

"Athletic's growth story and its mindset of improvement immediately caught my attention" , Maye said in the statement announcing his partnership with the brewery founded by Bill Shufelt and John Walker. Prescott, for his part, stated: "As I have become more involved in the business world, I have grown increasingly selective about the opportunities I pursue and the people I choose to work with".

articles.title: Cowboys defense branded ‘embarrassing’ after disastrous meltdown against Giants
articles.standfirst: Is it really the worst defense in the NFL? Cowboys face harsh criticism after nightmare Week 1 performance
articles.summary: Is it really the worst defense in the NFL? Cowboys face harsh criticism after nightmare Week 1 performance
articles.body:
The Dallas Cowboys were once again exposed by their defensive struggles during the 2026 NFL season . The unit’s promised transformation was called into question after a disastrous Week 1 performance, as the new defense under Christian Parker was dominated by the New York Giants and young quarterback Jaxson Dart .

The arrival of a new defensive coordinator, six new starters on the unit, and two first-round Draft picks focused on strengthening the defense had created optimism in Dallas. The expectation was that the team would move past the disaster of 2025 , when under Matt Eberflus , the Cowboys allowed 511 points , the highest total in the entire NFL.

However, it took just one game —a 28-20 loss to the Giants in the season opener— to raise the alarms again. The Cowboys’ defense showed many of the same issues from last season: a lack of response, poor adjustments, and an inability to stop opposing offenses.

The performance sparked heavy criticism around the league, with analysts and fans questioning the preparation, defensive approach, and Parker’s ability to handle such a significant responsibility.

At just 34 years old, Parker became the youngest defensive coordinator in franchise history. He arrived in Dallas after spending two seasons as the Philadelphia Eagles ’ defensive pass game coordinator and defensive backs coach, but his debut left plenty of doubts.

“It looks like a former secondary coach trying to be a defensive coordinator,” former NFL head coach and ESPN analyst Rex Ryan said on Get Up Monday morning. “Everything from the top down. It’s hilarious… somebody got outcoached.”

“One of the weirdest games you will ever see in your life,” NFL reporter John Frascella wrote on his official X account on Sunday night. “Giants keep running same play, same play, same play … Left flat, catch and run … and it keeps working over and over and over … Christian Parker and Cowboys D totally embarrassing themselves.”

Meanwhile, comedian and Cowboys fan Sal “Cousin Sal” Iacono also questioned the work of the new coordinator during the Bill Simmons Podcast.

“The Giants just kept running the same play over and over again,” Sal “Cousin Sal” Iacono said on The Bill Simmons Podcast Sunday night. “By the way, (Parker) could be an Eagles spy. We got him from Philadelphia, so he could be a double agent.”

The Cowboys made a major bet on Parker to rebuild the defense

Dallas made a major commitment to Parker as the person tasked with changing the direction of a defense that had been in crisis.

“The Cowboys are working to hire Eagles secondary coach and defensive pass game coordinator Christian Parker as their new defensive coordinator,” NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport wrote on January 22 . “The deal is not done, but hope is it will be. A rising young coach, he lands in a big spot with a rival.”

Parker took over the position after the firing of Matt Eberflus, who spent one season as Dallas’ defensive coordinator and left behind a unit that finished among the worst defenses in the entire NFL.

articles.title: Calls for Jerry Jones to finally relinquish control of the Cowboys: “He's selling the fans a fantasy”
articles.standfirst: Jones has owned the Cowboys since 1989 but has led them to just three Super Bowls.
articles.summary: Jones has owned the Cowboys since 1989 but has led them to just three Super Bowls.
articles.body:
The Dallas Cowboys ' latest defensive failure has reignited questions over Jerry Jones ' control of the franchise, with former receiver Terrell Owens arguing that the owner needs to step back. Jones entered the season insisting Dallas would field a stronger defense than the 2025 NFL season. That confidence quickly came under scrutiny after the Cowboys surrendered 28 points in a defeat to the New York Giants .

Owens criticized Jones following the loss, arguing that the Cowboys owner continues to present supporters with an unrealistic vision as his comments placed the owner's role at the center of the discussion. “It’s the same old same old,” Owens told Get To The Point. “I mean, Jerry Jones is really selling all these Cowboy fans, he’s selling them a fantasy, he’s selling them a dream. “He needs to relinquish some of the control that he has with the team and allow some other people to kind of step in place. “That’s kind of like a sign of narcissism, in a sense. And at the end of the day, he’s not even really worried about wins and losses.”

Cowboys' latest Super Bowl bid takes blow vs Giants

The criticism followed a performance that made Dallas ' defensive rebuild look uncertain as the Giants repeatedly exposed weaknesses. Cam Skattebo and Jaxson Dart proved able to effectively move the football on their way to beating the Cowboys ' revamped unit. Dallas had invested heavily in improving that defense during the offseason but despite the effort, New York converted nine of 11 third-down attempts. Von Miller was among the additions, while Christian Parke r took charge as coordinator after the unit struggled during the previous campaign. The Cowboys also added Caleb Downs , Malachi Lawrence , Jalen Thompson , Cobie Durant , Dee Winters and Rashan Gary . That 81.8% third down conversion represented the Giants ' strongest third-down showing since 1978, whilst Dallas only produced only the 21st-best pressure rate in Week 1 despite blitzing at the seventh-highest rate. The defensive struggles placed additional pressure on an offense featuring Dak Prescott , CeeDee Lamb , George Pickens and Javonte Williams . Even such a star-studded offense could not hide the defensive frailty as Dallas ultimately lost the game 28-20, starting the season with another setback.

The situation has renewed attention on how Jones operates the Cowboys compared to when he first acquired the franchise. Decades ago, he worked alongside Jimmy Johnson. Jones handled business matters while Johnson directed football operations. That arrangement helped Dallas win two Super Bowls , but the organization's structure has since evolved. Jones has remained deeply involved in football decisions while continuing as the team's owner and general manager - perhaps to the detriment of the franchise But regardless, the 83-year-old has shown little indication that he intends to relinquish control and claims he still has work to do as he pursues additional Super Bowl success. “I don’t have a succession plan, I don’t,” Jones told The Athletic. “One day I just won’t be here to toss my two cents in.” Jones is attempting to close the gap to Robert Kraft and the New England Patriots ' Super Bowl total. However, doing so would require four more championships - a tall order.
