articles.title: Brian Schottenheimer has identified those responsible for the Cowboys' loss to the Giants
articles.standfirst: Dallas suffered a 28-20 defeat in Week 1 of the 2026 NFL season.
articles.summary: Dallas suffered a 28-20 defeat in Week 1 of the 2026 NFL season.
articles.body:
The Dallas Cowboys left their season opener with more questions than answers, and Brian Schottenheimer was clear about where he believed the problems began after a 28-20 loss to the New York Giants . Dallas ' defense was expected to look different this season, but the numbers told a familiar story. The Cowboys surrendered 394 yards, including 165 rushing yards, while their own offense managed only 244.

Schottenheimer did not hide from those shortcomings when he addressed reporters. The head coach acknowledged that Dallas ' young defenders had made mistakes, while also accepting responsibility for how they were coached. "You know, one other thing, not an excuse, guys,” Schottenheimer said. “We did not play well. But you got young players, and young player closes and Jaxson Dart boots and gets outside. “We don’t push three different times to the [expletive] flat route. Excuse my language. You know, like, those are gonna happen. “And we have to coach the young players better, but when you play young players, it’s part of the deal. And they need to learn quickly.” The Cowboys repeatedly struggled to contain short throws into the flat, allowing the Giants to extend drives and keep pressure on a defense that spent much of the night trying to find answers. That urgency is understandable given how thoroughly the Giants controlled the game. New York held the ball for 36:40 compared with Dallas ' 23:20, while Dart helped enough offense to protect the lead. The Cowboys ' offense offered little resistance early, finishing with just 69 rushing yards and struggling to establish consistency. Two second-half touchdowns gave Dallas hope, but the comeback attempt arrived after too much damage had already been done. Caleb Downs provided one of the few encouraging performances among Dallas ' young players, but the rookie could not solve the wider problems alone. The Cowboys need more players to develop quickly if their rebuilt roster is to meet expectations.

Week 2 provides tough test as Cowboys chase opening win

The Cowboys do not have much time to dwell on the defeat, with the winless Washington Commanders next on the schedule. That matchup gives Dallas an opportunity to show whether the mistakes against the Giants were an opening-night stumble or a deeper concern. But it will not be easy. Washington may have opened the season with a loss, but they showed against the Philadelphia Eagles they cannot be judged on their record. They pushed the reigning NFC East champions to the brink before losing 24-22 as the Commanders trailed 24-16 with just over six minutes remaining, yet Jayden Daniels kept them alive with a late surge. He found Stefon Diggs for a touchdown to enter two-point conversion situation. However, a penalty on Diggs landed the team a 15-yard penalty and the chance to go for the two-point conversion failed. Eagles ' quarterback Jalen Hurts led the team downfield to score on the next drive to rub salt into the wounds. But Daniels was not done yet, connecting with rookie Antonio Williams for another score with 1:01 left and that final drive put Washington within one successful two-point conversion of forcing overtime. Although they did not make the conversion, Washington brought pressure, limited Philadelphia 's running game and recorded three sacks in a good performance. That performance should immediately concern Dallas when they meet the Commanders on the field on Sunday, September 20 after watching their own defense struggle against the run while failing to control the tempo.

articles.title: Micah Parsons is still thinking about the Dallas Cowboys, and he tries to inspire hope in their fans
articles.standfirst: Parsons is currently on the PUP list, awaiting his chance to make an impact for the Green Bay Packers.
articles.summary: Parsons is currently on the PUP list, awaiting his chance to make an impact for the Green Bay Packers.
articles.body:
The Dallas Cowboys losing their Week 1 game to the New York Giants , in a division game on the road, shouldn’t have most people batting an eye. But there was a surprising amount of hype coming out of Cowboys camp this summer.

In their second season under head coach Brian Schottenheimer , with an emphasis placed on improving the defense over the offseason, expectations were somewhat high for Dallas. That came to a screeching halt against the Giants; mostly because the defense didn’t look any better than last season, but also because the offense looked shockingly mediocre .

Micah Parsons says Dallas Cowboys have "too much talent" to not succeed in 2026

Cowboys fans are panicking a little bit, but one of the team’s former superstars isn’t sounding the alarm just yet. Micah Parsons , who was traded to the Green Bay Packers from Dallas just before the 2025 season, has indirectly implored Cowboys fans to not overreact to Week 1 . While speaking about Dallas’ loss on his podcast, Parsons explained why he thinks Week 1 may have been a fluke.

“ New [defensive coordinator], new players. One football camp can’t put it all together, bro. You can see [George Pickens], you know, wasn’t really himself yet. They have too much talent for it not to progress… GP won’t have a game like that again. That’s another one of them things where it’s like stats, they’ll deceive you .”

The Cowboys could have used Parsons on Sunday Night Football , although the defensive end is currently still going through the recovery process following a torn ACL and meniscus suffered last December. Parsons is currently on the PUP list , meaning he will miss the Packers’ first four games. There’s no firm date for his return just yet.

articles.summary: Dallas’ familiar defensive problems returned in a Week 1 loss to the New York Giants.
articles.body:
Terrell Owens believes Dak Prescott could thrive outside the Dallas Cowboys , where the pressure surrounding the team can be as demanding as the challenge of winning games.

His comments come after the team opened the 2026 NFL season with a 28-20 loss to the New York Giants , the team that finished fourth in the NFC East less than 12 months ago.

And when asked whether Prescott could succeed with another franchise, Owens replied with confidence.

“I think so, Owens told the Get To The Point show. “Again, when you play with the Dallas Cowboys, there’s so many expectations. Obviously, historic franchise. I don’t know the last time they won a Super Bowl.”

Owens also noted that Dallas has endured seasons when expectations were high, but the results fell short and believes that unless they improve their time of possession allowed, then it could be a difficult year.

Prescott struggles in Week 1 loss to New York Giants

Prescott finished the opener with 175 passing yards, two touchdowns and an interception but that is partially due to the fact that his star receivers also had an uneven afternoon.

George Pickens dropped two important passes, including one that preceded the interception, while CeeDee Lamb dropped three to result in a difficult start for an offense that is backed as a Super Bowl contender.

But away from offensive struggles, the defense remains the larger concern as Dallas ranked last in the league defensively in the 2025 NFL season below even the 3-14 Las Vegas Raiders , and its Week 1 showing offered little reassurance.

Despite the arrival of new defensive coordinator Christian Parker and additions to the roster, the Cowboys blitzed at the league’s seventh-highest rate but ranked 21st in pressure rate against the Giants .

The defense recorded two sacks on Jaxson Dart , one credited to rookie safety Caleb Downs , while allowing New York to gain 394 yards as Dart threw for 230 yards and three touchdowns without an interception.

The Giants controlled the ball for much of the game and the result left Dallas facing familiar questions about whether its defense can support Prescott consistently.

“It sucks to lose, it damn sure sucks to lose the first one, to this team,” Prescott said. “A division game, but still optimistic.

“That doesn’t change our goals, that doesn’t change how we feel about our team. As I said, credit to those guys. They beat us.”

Prescott and the Cowboys now turn to the Washington Commanders on September 20, and Dallas faces immediate task to find answers on both sides of the ball in another NFC East match-up.

articles.title: Jerry Jones sends Cowboys fans a defiant message about Super Bowl hopes
articles.standfirst: The Dallas Cowboys owner isn't giving up on his team after just one game.
articles.summary: The Dallas Cowboys owner isn't giving up on his team after just one game.
articles.body:
It wasn't quite the start to the 2026 NFL season that the Dallas Cowboys were anticipating in Week 1. Playing a division rival on the road shouldn't be considered an overly negative development, but Dallas had built up a lot of hope with a strong offseason.

But in the team's season opener against the New York Giants , similar weaknesses from a season ago came back to haunt them. Naturally, that has analysts and fans souring on the potential for the Cowboys this season. Considered to be a dark horse Super Bowl contender for some, those high expectations have now fully been checked.

Jerry Jones is always optimistic about his Dallas Cowboys

Don't tell that to Cowboys owner Jerry Jones , though. Ever the optimist, Jones needs to only look back one season in order to inspire hope for himself and for Cowboys fans. A loss in Week 1 isn't deterring Jones from fortifying his Super Bowl aspirations .

I'll go to the two teams that played in the Super Bowl last year. They both lost their opening games. Both teams were put together, actually, from the back down. They surprisingly didn't have the continuity that you might expect a Super Bowl to have. ​ ​But both of those teams lost their opening game. Both of them evolved as the season went along. Bear in mind, it's important — I've lost a game and won the Super Bowl.

Jones referenced his 1993 Cowboys team , which lost the opening game then went on to win the Super Bowl. In fact, they were the first team in NFL history to start a season 0-2 and win the Lombardi Trophy in the same season. The 2001 New England Patriots and 2007 New York Giants later joined that club.

articles.title: Dak Prescott fires back at panicking Cowboys Nation after embarrassing Week 1 flop
articles.standfirst: Dak Prescott had a message for frustrated Cowboys fans after Dallas opened the season with a loss.
articles.summary: Dak Prescott had a message for frustrated Cowboys fans after Dallas opened the season with a loss.
articles.body:
D ak Prescott understands the frustration of Dallas Cowboys fans after another difficult start, but the quarterback made it clear he is not about to panic after just one week of the season.

Following the 28-20 loss to the New York Giants in Week 1 , Prescott was asked about the mood of a fan base that fears 2026 could follow the same path as recent seasons, with Dallas missing the playoffs for a second straight year.

His response was a call for calm

“I mean, it’s a long season. I love our fans, but I don’t necessarily feel like I need to speak to that fan. Sorry for them. If they’re a real fan, they’ll stick with it. They’ll trust it. They’ll believe in it. And at the end of the day, it is one game. Yeah, it sucks, it’s the first game.”

The quarterback stressed that the disappointment inside the locker room runs deeper than anything the fans are feeling, because no one expected to open the season with a loss.

“Nobody’s more pissed than myself and these guys in here. We didn’t want to start 0-1. We’re as excited as any fan out there about the offseason and things we’ve done in training camp. So turn that energy and come to the game this Sunday and be as loud as you can. We appreciate it.”

The Cowboys entered the new year with high expectations behind an offense led by Prescott, CeeDee Lamb, George Pickens and Javonte Williams . But that unit fell well short of its potential against New York.

Dallas now has an immediate chance to rewrite the narrative when it faces the Washington Commanders .

One of the more scrutinized players was George Pickens , who endured a rough debut in a Cowboys uniform. The wide receiver finished with just three catches for 28 yards and dropped two key passes . The most costly came in the first half when he was wide open behind the Giants’ secondary on a potential touchdown and failed to haul it in.

Prescott was far from sharp himself. He completed the day with 175 yards, two touchdowns and an interception — numbers that fell short of the lofty expectations surrounding Dallas’ offense.

While a Week 1 loss does not define an entire season, another defeat inside the division could quickly ratchet up the pressure o n a Cowboys team determined to return to the playoff picture.

articles.title: Troy Aikman is very concerned about the Cowboys' defense: “A little bit alarming”
articles.standfirst: The Dallas Cowboys surrendered 28 points to the New York Giants in Week 1.
articles.summary: The Dallas Cowboys surrendered 28 points to the New York Giants in Week 1.
articles.body:
The Dallas Cowboys were supposed to have turned the page on their defensive struggles but instead, Troy Aikman is already raising a familiar warning sign after a troubling Week 1 showing. The Cowboys invested heavily in the unit, adding Quinnen Williams , Cobie Durant , Jaishawn Barham , Rashan Gary , Caleb Downs , Malachi Lawrence and Von Miller - yet the changes offered little against New York Giants as the team gave up 28 points.

Dallas had entered the season with renewed expectations after rebuilding a defense that surrendered 30.1 points per game but their defeat to the Giants is sparking fears of another tough year, and Aikman did not hide his concern. “A little bit alarming,” Aikman told 97.1 The Ticket’s The Musers. “And it always is more pronounced in Week 1, because there’s so much attention and so much time to prepare. “As soon as the season’s schedule comes out, you know who you’re going to be playing, and you’ve got all offseason to kind of get prepared for that opener. And when it doesn’t go as you hope, then it just adds a lot of angst.” Dallas simply did not deliver when expectations were high as the Giants repeatedly controlled the game on third down, converting nine of 11 attempts as their success kept the Cowboys defense on the field and allowed New York to dictate the tempo. The offense was good when it had the chance to get on the ball as the team scored 21 points through Dak Prescott , Javonte Williams , Ceedee Lamb and George Pickens but it wasn’t enough.

Can the Cowboys find an answer in Week 2?

Surrendering 394 total yards and allowing two second-half touchdown drives each consumed roughly eight minutes and ensured the offense could not transform the fortunes – although Downs supplied one of two sacks. The early numbers have created uncomfortable comparisons with last season, when Dallas finished with the NFL ’s worst scoring defense and now the new coordinator Christian Parker now faces pressure to show his changes can work. And that next opponent brings added urgency as since the 1970 merger, only 10 percent of teams that started 0-2 ultimately reached the NFL Playoffs , making the Week 2 response especially important. But Parker has refused to dismiss the defeat, instead demanding accountability before the Cowboys face the Washington Commanders . “It’s one poor performance,” Parker said. “It’s one loss that does not equal two. I think we’re not trying to make excuses for anything. We’re not trying to act like it didn’t happen. “We got to look in the mirror, we got to be accountable for what we did wrong and what we did right, correct it and then move on to the next opponent because it can’t be a hangover and it can’t linger.” The Cowboys will take on the Washington on Sunday, September 20 at the AT&T Stadium from 16:30 ET/13:30 PT. The Commanders enter after narrowly losing to Philadelphia Eagles 24-22 in Week 1.

articles.title: Cowboys offensive coordinator sets his sights on Pittsburgh as Dallas continues to struggle
articles.standfirst: Dallas has barely begun the season, and the Cowboys already have something to say about the work one of their players received in Pittsburgh.
articles.summary: Dallas has barely begun the season, and the Cowboys already have something to say about the work one of their players received in Pittsburgh.
articles.body:
T he Cowboys did not get the debut they expected, and while they are still trying to find answers after their first game , a situation that began far from Dallas ended up putting the spotlight on one of their new players.

The season began with a 28-20 loss to the New York Giants , a result that brought some of the questions surrounding the team in 2025 back to the table.

The defense was one of the biggest problems. The Giants finished with 394 total yards, including 165 on the ground , and converted nine of their 11 third-down attempts.

But Dallas did not leave the game with good news in other areas either. Communication issues and some poor reads led to mistakes, while injuries to Malik Hooker and DeMarvion Overshown left even more work to do before Week 2 .

With all of that on the table, the Cowboys already had plenty to fix. However, the arrival of Broderick Jones opened up a different conversation, one that is not only about what the tackle can do in Dallas , but also about what happened before he got there.

Jones arrived in Dallas from the Steelers during cutdown day, but from the start, it was clear that the Cowboys could not simply put him on the line and expect immediate results.

The team had already made it clear that the tackle would have to adjust to certain differences between the techniques he learned in Pittsburgh and what Dallas expects from him .

Now, Klayton Adams, Dallas' offensive coordinator, addressed the subject again before a practice. And one of his comments took the conversation in a different direction.

Adams explained that the physical part of the process would take time, something that can be expected from a player who has just joined a new team. But then he added: “Not sure how those things fell through the cracks where he was at.”

And that's the detail that stands out.

The comment drew attention because Adams was no longer talking only about what Jones needs to learn with the Cowboys. He was also pointing to certain things that, according to Adams, were not where the team expected them to be when the player arrived in Dallas .

The Cowboys also do not appear willing to wait too long to start seeing progress. Adams made it clear that the team expected to see a significant change already.

Jones and his adjustment process

During his time with the Steelers, Jones struggled to establish himself, and he himself pointed to one of the factors that made the process more difficult: constantly switching between left and right tackle .

“Bouncing around positions” was how he described the situation, explaining that not being able to settle on one side made it harder to feel comfortable and get familiar with the players around him.

Dallas has taken a different approach.

The plan now is for Jones to focus on right tackle, compete for the position and have the opportunity to become familiar with one spot. The team does not appear interested in repeating the dynamic that the player himself identified as a challenge during his time in Pittsburgh .

Now Dallas has to show what Jones can do

Adams' comments may raise questions about how Jones was developed before arriving in Dallas, but the most important part will begin when the player has to show what he can do with this new opportunity.

And while the Cowboys look for answers after falling to 0-1 , they will also have to find out whether everything they are trying to change with Broderick Jones can turn into results.

The next test will come against the Washington Commanders .

articles.title: Dallas Cowboys continue to face problems: Two more players injured before facing the Commanders
articles.standfirst: Dallas faces more adversity before NFC East showdown
articles.summary: Dallas faces more adversity before NFC East showdown
articles.body:
The Dallas Cowboys will enter Sunday’s NFC East clash with the Washington Commanders dealing with another defensive headache.

After opening the 2026 season with a 28-20 loss to the New York Giants, Dallas has confirmed that two defensive starters won’t be available for its home opener.

Linebacker DeMarvion Overshown and safety Malik Hooker have both been ruled out after suffering injuries in Week 1. Hooker fractured his forearm and underwent surgery, while Overshown is recovering from a hamstring strain.

Cowboys head coach Brian Schottenheimer has indicated that neither injury is expected to become a long-term problem, with Hooker potentially returning in about two weeks and Overshown expected to miss roughly one to two weeks.

Neither player has been placed on injured reserve, which further suggests the Cowboys expect both defenders to return relatively soon. Still, their absence creates an immediate challenge for a defense that struggled to limit the Giants during the season opener.

Dallas will now have to rely on several younger players and reshuffle responsibilities across the unit. That could make Sunday’s divisional matchup an early opportunity for some of the Cowboys’ less experienced defenders to establish themselves.

Cowboys reshuffle defense for Washington matchup

Rookie linebacker Jaishawn Barham is expected to take over at middle linebacker and handle the green-dot communication duties against Washington.

That role requires him to relay defensive calls and help organize the unit before each snap, giving the rookie an important responsibility just one game into his NFL career.

At safety, P.J. Locke is expected to take on additional work with Hooker sidelined. Dallas isn’t simply planning to move first-round pick Caleb Downs into Hooker’s role, however.

The coaching staff views Downs as particularly valuable closer to the line of scrimmage, where his versatility can be used in different ways.

There’s some encouraging news elsewhere on the Cowboys’ injury report. Outside linebacker James Houston and offensive lineman Ajani Cornelius practiced fully Friday and entered the weekend without a game-status designation. Their availability gives Dallas some additional depth heading into the matchup.

The offense will also be expected to respond after an inconsistent opening performance. CeeDee Lamb caught a touchdown against the Giants and remains one of the Cowboys’ biggest offensive weapons.

“I know the city gonna be rocking. The game is gonna be fire. I can’t wait to just go out there and have everybody excited, score a couple of touchdowns and blow the roof off the place,” said Lamb ahead of the matchup.

Washington also enters the matchup at 0-1 following its 24-22 loss to Philadelphia. With both NFC East rivals looking for their first victory, Sunday’s meeting carries added importance despite arriving so early in the season.

articles.title: Cowboys owner Jerry Jones makes a stunning admission following Dallas disappointing season opener
articles.standfirst: Following this week's game against Washington, the Cowboys will play in Brazil in Week 3
articles.summary: Following this week's game against Washington, the Cowboys will play in Brazil in Week 3
articles.body:
The 2026 NFL season did not start well for the Dallas Cowboys , who were thoroughly dominated by the New York Giants in a 28-20 defeat. The Giants controlled the clock for a staggering 36:40 minutes of game time, starving the Cowboys' offense of opportunities and limiting them to just two possessions in the entire second half.

This opening stumble proved that "America's Team" still carries glaring defensive vulnerabilities from a dismal campaign a year ago, where Dallas allowed more than 20 points in all but one game, surrendered 30 or more points in nine separate contests , and ranked dead last in franchise history for points allowed per drive.

Offensively, the squad struggled to find any rhythm as quarterback Dak Prescott managed just 175 passing yards, while the ground attack sputtered and finished with fewer than 70 total yards.

Jerry Jones Stark Admission After Cowboys' Disappointing Loss

Following the sobering defeat, outspoken Cowboys owner and general manager Jerry Jones appeared on Dallas radio station "105.3 The Fan" on Friday to deliver a remarkably candid assessment of his team's shortcomings.

Jones admitted that Dallas drastically underperformed while acknowledging that the Giants simply outplayed expectations. "They just did a good job all over," Jones confessed . "And I will tell you, they were better than we thought they were. We didn’t play as well as we should play and can play, but they played better than I thought they could."

When directly pressed on whether the Cowboys themselves are simply not as talented as anticipated , Jones conceded the point with a stark warning to the coaching staff and roster, noting that the squad is currently operating well below its envisioned standard.

Pointing to the massive scale of the franchise's offseason roster overhaul as a primary contributor to the sluggish start, Jones watched as his team self-destructed with eight penalties costing 85 yards , complementing a defense that yielded 28 points.

Second year head coach Brian Schottenheimer didn't mince words either, describing the overall execution as "pretty poor" in the aftermath.

Eager to wipe the slate clean, the Cowboys are packing their bags and returning home for Week 2, where they will host the division-rival Washington Commanders on Sunday inside AT&T Stadium for their highly anticipated home opener.

Jerry Jones Stark Admission After Cowboys' Disappointing Loss

Following the sobering defeat, outspoken Cowboys owner and general manager Jerry Jones appeared on Dallas radio station "105.3 The Fan" on Friday to deliver a remarkably candid assessment of his team's shortcomings.

Jones admitted that Dallas drastically underperformed while acknowledging that the Giants simply outplayed expectations. "They just did a good job all over," Jones confessed . "And I will tell you, they were better than we thought they were. We didn’t play as well as we should play and can play, but they played better than I thought they could."

When directly pressed on whether the Cowboys themselves are simply not as talented as anticipated , Jones conceded the point with a stark warning to the coaching staff and roster, noting that the squad is currently operating well below its envisioned standard.

Pointing to the massive scale of the franchise's offseason roster overhaul as a primary contributor to the sluggish start, Jones watched as his team self-destructed with eight penalties costing 85 yards , complementing a defense that yielded 28 points.
Second year head coach Brian Schottenheimer didn't mince words either, describing the overall execution as "pretty poor" in the aftermath.

Eager to wipe the slate clean, the Cowboys are packing their bags and returning home for Week 2, where they will host the division-rival Washington Commanders on Sunday inside AT&T Stadium for their highly anticipated home opener.

articles.title: Commanders vs Cowboys: Where to watch Dallas' game in NFL Week 2 and game time against Washington
articles.standfirst: Cowboys and Commanders face off in Week 2 seeking their first victory at AT&T Stadium
articles.summary: Cowboys and Commanders face off in Week 2 seeking their first victory at AT&T Stadium
articles.body:
The oldest rivalry in the NFC East is reignited in NFL Week 2, and it comes with an unusual twist: both the Dallas Cowboys and the Washington Commanders start 0-1, and both need to respond before the start of the season becomes even more complicated.

This Sunday, at AT&T Stadium in Arlington, two offenses capable of scoring in bunches will clash with divisional pride on the line.

Neither of the two delivered in Week 1. Dallas fell on the road to the New York Giants 20-28, a stumble in which Dak Prescott's offense got bogged down despite piling up volume: the quarterback completed 22 of 34 passes for 175 yards, with 2 touchdowns but also 1 interception and just 5.1 yards per attempt.

The Giants dominated the ball with 36:40 of possession compared to Dallas's 23:20, and rushed for 165 yards to the visitors' 69: a physical imbalance that the Cowboys urgently need to correct.

Washington, meanwhile, opened with a 22-24 loss to the Philadelphia Eagles, the conference champions last season. Jayden Daniels went 18 of 34 for 164 yards and 2 touchdowns without interceptions, and added 31 rushing yards on 5 carries. It was a hard-fought game until the end that the Commanders were close to stealing.

Recent history between the Commanders vs Cowboys

These two teams know each other by heart, and the most recent matchups confirm it. In the 2025-2026 season they faced each other three times, Dallas won two of the last three, although the margins tell a story of trading blows; the results were:

Commanders 23 - 19 Cowboys

Cowboys 44 - 22 Commanders

Cowboys 30 -23 Commanders

Kickoff time and where to watch the Commanders vs Cowboys game

The matchup between Dallas and Washington is scheduled for this Sunday, with kickoff set for 4:25 p.m. Eastern Time (3:25 p.m. Central Time and 1:25 p.m. Pacific Time.

Regarding the game broadcast, it will be on FOX with the option to watch it via streaming on FOX One. Internationally, the Commanders vs. Cowboys matchup can be followed with NFL Game Pass International, through DAZN.

Commanders vs Cowboys: Players to watch

On the Dallas side, CeeDee Lamb remains the engine of the offense: he caught 5 receptions for 44 yards and a touchdown in Week 1, leading the team with 8 targets.

The addition of George Pickens (3 catches, 28 yards) gives Prescott another vertical threat, while Javonte Williams shined as a dual weapon with a rushing and receiving touchdown.

On defense, linebacker DeMarvion Overshown led the hunt with 7 solo tackles, and kicker Brandon Aubrey is always a source of guaranteed points.

For Washington, the receiving duo looks promising: Stefon Diggs was targeted the most with 9 targets, 4 receptions, 55 yards, and a touchdown, while Antonio Williams contributed 64 yards and another score with an efficient 16 yards per reception.

Rookie running back Jacory Croskey-Merritt rushed for 63 yards and a touchdown on 16 carries, showing signs that Washington wants a reliable ground game around Daniels. Also keep an eye on Frankie Luvu, who contributed a sack and constant pressure from the linebacker position.

What's at stake in the NFC East division

The NFC East arrived at this week tightly contested. The Giants and the Eagles opened 1-0 and share the top spot, while the Commanders and Cowboys carry the 0-1 label. Losing this head-to-head matchup would mean not only falling to 0-2, but doing so within the division, with the tiebreaker disadvantage in the mix.

It is, in practical terms, a four-point game: the winner moves to 1-1 and jumps right into the conversation; the loser is left on the ropes very early in a division that shows no mercy.

How is the betting market and what is the prediction for Commanders vs Cowboys?

Sportsbooks see Dallas as a clear home favorite: the Cowboys are priced at 1.52 (an implied probability of 64.8%) on the moneyline, compared to Washington’s 2.86 (35.2%). The point spread has Dallas at -3.5 at 1.90, and the total points line is around 50.5-51.5, reflecting that the market expects a high-scoring afternoon between two offenses that know how to move the chains.

Home-field advantage and Prescott's efficiency with two elite receivers tip the balance toward the Cowboys, but Washington has the most dangerous weapon for stealing a game: Jayden Daniels' mobility and a receiving corps led by Diggs. If Dallas doesn't fix its run defense —where it struggled in Week 1—, Croskey-Merritt and Daniels could have them scrambling all afternoon.

Prediction: Dallas prevails in a close, high-scoring game, something like 30-27, powered by Aubrey’s leg and a Prescott-Lamb connection that shows up in the key moments. But don’t expect Washington to give up: this rivalry has all the makings of being decided in the final minutes.

articles.title: Week 2 Warning: Jerry Jones speaks out before pivotal Commanders matchup
articles.standfirst: The Cowboys owner was in a playful mood even as Dallas faced an important early-season test
articles.summary: The Cowboys owner was in a playful mood even as Dallas faced an important early-season test
articles.body:
Jerry Jones found time for a little rivalry banter before the Dallas Cowboys ’ first home game of the season, even with his team already facing pressure to respond after a disappointing opener.

As Jones made his way through the tunnel at AT&T Stadium before Sunday’s NFC East matchup against the Washington Commanders , he stopped to acknowledge supporters and spotted one fan wearing Washington colors.

“Tell 'em to be sweet to us,” Jones said. The exchange was lighthearted, but the stakes surrounding the game are not.

Dallas entered Week 2 looking to avoid an 0-2 start after a 28-20 loss to the New York Giants , a result that immediately put renewed focus on a defense that struggled to contain New York in key situations.

Washington, also searching for its first win, offered the Cowboys little room for another slow start.

Giants were better than expected

Jones had already created headlines earlier in the week by acknowledging that New York exceeded his expectations in the opener.

“They were better than how we thought they were,” Jones told 105.3 The Fan. “They played better than we thought they could.”

That assessment stood out given Dallas ’ own recent history. The Cowboys missed the playoffs in each of the previous two seasons and entered 2026 hoping that changes made on defense would help them re-establish themselves as a serious NFC contender.

Jones , however, is expecting improvement against Washington: “The improvement from where we played on Sunday [on defense] will be there,” he said. “I'll go on record saying that.”

His confidence puts added attention on a unit that showed familiar problems in Week 1, including a lack of pressure and communication breakdowns.

Cowboys know home opener carries more weight

Jones also made clear that Sunday’s game feels more important because of how poorly Dallas opened the season.

“This one is particularly challenging, not challenging, exciting if you will because we really did not do what we wanted to do in our opening game there in New York,” he said.

“This puts added emphasis on this game. We really want to play well in front of our home fans.”

Jones may have joked about wanting Washington to “be sweet,” but Dallas knows it cannot rely on favors. A stronger defensive performance and a cleaner overall showing are needed if the Cowboys are going to move past Week 1 quickly.

The rivalry adds another layer. Dallas and Washington have spent decades trading blows inside the NFC East, and even an early-season meeting can carry more emotion than its place on the calendar might suggest.

Jones ’ tunnel message drew smiles. What happens once the ball is kicked off will matter far more.

articles.title: Jake Ferguson and the Cowboys finally give Haley Cavinder and fans a Sunday to celebrate
articles.standfirst: Jake Ferguson’s wife returned to the stands to watch him play for Dallas, but this time the afternoon ended very differently.
articles.summary: Jake Ferguson’s wife returned to the stands to watch him play for Dallas, but this time the afternoon ended very differently.
articles.body:
T he Dallas Cowboys appear to have responded quickly after the nightmare they experienced in Week 1 against the New York Giants . The team entered its second game of the season with several of the problems that had already been exposed during 2025 still on the table, but this Sunday, Dallas found a convincing answer at home with a 37-20 win over the Washington Commanders.

The difference was not just on the scoreboard. Dallas showed a much more consistent offense, did not turn the ball over and got four touchdown passes from Dak Prescott , while the defense also made adjustments after a difficult start to the season. And in the middle of that turnaround, a familiar face returned to the spotlight: Haley Cavinder, Jake Ferguson’s wife .

This time, however, No. 87 had a much happier afternoon.

Haley returned to the stands to support Jake

The influencer and former basketball player showed up wearing beige-fringed denim pants , paired with a cropped top and a brown belt featuring the No. 87 at the center, Ferguson’s jersey number with Dallas.

She completed the outfit with brown open-toe heels and wore her hair down, keeping a look that mixed casual pieces with a few more polished details.

And while the outfit already featured a clear reference to Ferguson, what happened a few hours later gave that 87 even more meaning .

No. 87 finally had a reason to celebrate

Ferguson quickly became part of the story.

The Cowboys tight end finished with 4 receptions for 43 yards and 2 touchdowns , becoming one of the key pieces of Dallas’ offense during the win.

Both touchdowns came through the air and marked a significant difference from what happened in the season opener, when Ferguson finished with just 2 receptions for 6 yards against the Giants .

Prescott also had a day to remember

Dallas’ offense found much more consistency this time, led by Dak Prescott , who finished with four touchdown passes.

His performance also carried special significance for the franchise. With those touchdown passes, he broke the Cowboys’ franchise record for passing touchdowns .

CeeDee Lamb also contributed to the offensive production, while the defense recorded two sacks and limited Washington’s rushing attack.

On the other side, the Commanders also had to deal with the departure of Jayden Daniels , who suffered a left elbow injury on the final play of the first half. Marcus Mariota then took over for the remainder of the game.

The Cowboys will have little time to enjoy the turnaround, with Week 3 already on the horizon.

Dallas will return to action on Sunday, September 27, 2026 , when the team hosts the Baltimore Ravens in its next game of the season.

articles.title: Lone Star Legend: Dak Prescott shatters Tony Romo's record and becomes the Cowboys' all-time king
articles.standfirst: Dak Prescott's four-touchdown performance against Washington pushed him past Tony Romo and into first place on the Cowboys' all-time passing touchdowns list
articles.summary: Dak Prescott's four-touchdown performance against Washington pushed him past Tony Romo and into first place on the Cowboys' all-time passing touchdowns list
articles.body:
D ak Prescott has officially written his name at the top of another major Dallas Cowboys record, surpassing Tony Romo to become the franchise's all-time leader in touchdown passes.

The milestone arrived during Sunday's 37-20 victory over the Washington Commanders at AT&T Stadium. Prescott entered the afternoon needing one touchdown pass to move beyond Romo's mark of 248, and he ultimately finished with four scoring throws, taking his career total to 249.

The record-breaking play came late in the fourth quarter, when Prescott connected with CeeDee Lamb for a 24-yard touchdown.

It was the second touchdown connection between the quarterback and wide receiver on the afternoon and gave Prescott sole possession of the franchise record.

For Prescott , the achievement represented the culmination of a belief he had carried since childhood.

“Sometimes it’s great being naïve, and I was a little naïve just growing up thinking that I could do this and I could do that, but yet I think it puts such an insurmountable belief in my head that I can accomplish whatever I want to accomplish,” Prescott said after the match.

“And any thought that I said or anything that I wanted to do, I mentioned it and I said it out loud. I had a mom and I had brothers who poured gas on those thoughts, who told me I could. And as I said, you can call it arrogance, you can call it confidence, belief, whatever you need to. I wouldn’t be here if I didn’t have those thoughts, if I didn’t believe in myself like that.”

The quarterback's words also reflected the significance of the people who helped him reach the NFL.

Prescott grew up in Haughton, Louisiana, and was selected by Dallas in the fourth round of the 2016 NFL Draft. Ten seasons later, he has moved past one of the most prominent quarterbacks in franchise history.

Romo's 248 touchdown passes had stood as the Cowboys ' benchmark, but Prescott has now taken the record for himself.

Prescott's record night delivers a much-needed Cowboys victory

The individual achievement was accompanied by an important result for Dallas. Prescott completed 26 of 31 passes for 279 yards and four touchdowns, producing a passer rating of 143.8 as the Cowboys earned their first victory of the 2026 season and moved to 1-1.

CeeDee Lamb was central to the performance, catching eight passes for 153 yards and two touchdowns. Jake Ferguson also caught two touchdown passes from Prescott , giving the quarterback four different scoring connections during the game.

The victory also marked another strong performance by Prescott against Washington at home. He entered the contest with a 7-0 record against the Commanders in Dallas and maintained that unbeaten mark with Sunday's result.

Cowboys owner Jerry Jones praised the work that Prescott puts in away from the spotlight, emphasizing that the record is the product of years of preparation.

“I just think it’s such a statement for how he did it, how he does it,” Jones said. “And he does it with hard, hard work. And he makes it look pretty easy out there. But anybody that knows … you guys that see him at practice and training camp [know] that he’s the hardest-working guy on the team. So I’m proud for him.”

Prescott , meanwhile, made it clear that he does not view 249 as a finishing point.

“I want to double it,” Prescott said. “Plan on playing for a while. So just getting started.”

That ambition could put further distance between Prescott and Romo in the coming seasons. Prescott has already established himself as the Cowboys ' leader in passing touchdowns, and his next targets include other significant marks across the franchise's record book.

His record-breaking afternoon also came with a personal element. Prescott said after the game that he felt the presence of his late mother, Peggy, during the touchdown that put him at the top of the Cowboys' list.

He also used the moment to encourage young people who may not have the same resources or circumstances as others: “And I just encourage the next little kid out there who comes from the trailer park in Louisiana or wherever he may come from and doesn’t know if he can do it or have the resources or have the family that you’re right, believe in what you want to believe in and find the people that support that, and you can do it.”

Prescott's record is now official: 249 touchdown passes and counting. After a decade in Dallas, the quarterback has moved past Romo and taken another place of prominence in Cowboys history. And if his own words are any indication, he intends to keep adding to the number.

Jerry Jones had a message for the rest of the NFL after the Dallas Cowboys earned their first victory of the season.

Following Dallas’ 37-20 win over the Washington Commanders, the Cowboys owner approached reporters and delivered a line that immediately went viral.

Jones offered no further explanation, but the timing left fans wondering whether he was simply celebrating the dominant win or hinting that another major move could be coming. Either way, the 83-year-old owner made one thing clear: he believes the Cowboys are far from finished.

articles.title: “There’s nothing more dangerous than an old man with money”: Jerry Jones has a warning for the Cowboys
articles.standfirst: Jones knows the Cowboys bounced back in a big way after losing in Week 1 to the Giants
articles.summary: Jones knows the Cowboys bounced back in a big way after losing in Week 1 to the Giants
articles.body:
Cowboys owner Jerry Jones had every reason to be pleased with the team's 37-20 victory, having stayed remarkably calm following the opening-week loss to the Giants by reminding everyone, "I've lost the first game (1993) and won the Super Bowl." Knowing that this campaign carries a strict Super Bowl or bust mandate per Dak Prescott’s own words, securing victories early is vital for the franchise's championship aspirations.

Following the final whistle against Washington, Jones approached reporters at his customary postgame tunnel spot and dropped a meticulously crafted line: "There is nothing more dangerous than an old man with money," Jones stated. "That is my quote for the day." ( See video below )

The provocative statement quintessential of the billionaire owner highlights an underlying urgency for the remainder of the year. With plenty of football left, Jones may look to orchestrate a mid-season trade to reinforce a roster that packs an explosive offensive punch but still requires defensive upgrades after enduring back-to-back difficult defensive campaigns.

An Historic Dak Prescott and a Brutal October Stretch

It was an excellent Sunday in Dallas with the Cowboys winning 37-20 against the Washington Commanders to avoid a dreaded 0-2 start to the season, as they now prepare to travel to Brazil for a high-profile matchup against the Baltimore Ravens on Sunday afternoon.

Getting the job done mattered most, regardless of style points, though the victory was influenced by Washington quarterback Jayden Daniels exiting the game due to an injury on the final play of the second half.

The defining takeaway from the contest belonged to Dak Prescott , who dazzled by throwing for 279 passing yards and four touchdown passes , bringing his career total to 249 passing scores and officially surpassing Tony Romo for the most passing touchdowns in franchise history .

Alongside his standing as the organization’s all-time leader in passing yards , Prescott can now stake a strong claim as the greatest regular-season quarterback in team history, though scrutiny remains high regarding his postseason resume given his 2-5 playoff record across 10 seasons.

Following their upcoming international trip to battle the Ravens, the Cowboys face a grueling October slate featuring a road test against the Houston Texans , a home clash against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers on Thursday Night Football, and tough away dates in Green Bay and Philadelphia .

If Dallas navigates this upcoming five-game gauntlet with a positive record, they will undoubtedly cement their status among the elite contenders in the NFC .

articles.title: Jerry Jones goes out of character with effusive praise for Dak Prescott as Cowboys Super Bowl hopes return
articles.standfirst: Jones is fully invested in his franchise quarterback as Dallas rebounds from Week 1.
articles.summary: Jones is fully invested in his franchise quarterback as Dallas rebounds from Week 1.
articles.body:
Perhaps no team in the NFL had a more important rebound than the Dallas Cowboys in Week 2. After looking totally out of sync in their Week 1 loss to the New York Giants , the Cowboys dismantled their other NFC East rivals, the Washington Commanders , in Week 2.

Playing at home surely helped, as did Washington quarterback Jayden Daniels going down with an injury, but the Cowboys offense looked much more like its usual self in Week 2. Quarterback Dak Prescott , in particular, was simply outstanding. Prescott completed 26-of-31 pass attempts for 279 yards and four touchdowns . It was the kind of performance that has Cowboys owner Jerry Jones dreaming of a Super Bowl once again.

Jerry Jones says Dak Prescott can be the best QB in the NFL and win a Super Bowl for the Cowboys

Jones admitted as much on his weekly local radio appearance for 105.3 The Fan . While gleaming with positivity, Jones couldn't help but praise Prescott in a way that even surprised Cowboys fans .

I think he's the poster child of any players I've been around. Of what you can do to self-improve. And he's a product of his own work ethic. He's a product of his focus on getting better every detail of his game. I'm happy to say that he is a better quarterback today than he's ever been. ​ ​It's a position that if you approach it the he's approached his career, you will be a better player. I'm glad we've got him... How he got where he is, is to me a noteworthy leg on his chair of being the best. He could be the best out there as far as I'm concerned.

Jones went on to add that Prescott performing at " an extremely high level " gives the team " our best chance" to win a Super Bowl . The tune and vibes around the Cowboys have certainly shifted dramatically following their Week 1 setback.
